title: Manipulating Li2MnO3-Like Domain Dispersion in Lithium-Rich Layered Oxides Inherited from Precursor
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Leveraging oxygen redox in lithium-rich layered oxides paves the way for increasing the energy density of lithium-ion batteries, whose practical implementation is plagued by poor stability. Although a uniform Li2MnO3-like domain dispersion is suggested to improve cycle stability, the synthesis–structure relationship governing domain formation remains underexplored. Here, we show that Li2MnO3-like domain dispersion is derived by the precursor structure according to the degree of transition-metal separation. Through a comparative investigation of the synthesis mechanism, we reveal the templating effect that more clustered transition-metal oxide precursors lead to more localized Li2MnO3-like ordering in the final cathodes, a tendency also observed with a different lithium source. Furthermore, it is corroborated that cathodes with more dispersed Li2MnO3-like ordering derived from less-ordered precursors exhibit improved electrochemical stability with a mitigated voltage decay. Our findings highlight the significance of precursor design and engineering for structural regulation of high-performance lithium-rich layered oxide cathodes.

title: Bridging microwaves and light
abstract: Strong coupling between magnons and excitons in CrSBr enables microwave-to-optical transduction, offering a route towards efficient conversion between otherwise disparate frequency regimes.

title: Rational Integration of Multiple Additives for High-Temperature Lithium-Ion Batteries
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The rational combination of multiple electrolyte additives is a promising strategy for constructing stable interphases in lithium-ion batteries. However, unintended additive interactions can alter the preferential reduction/oxidation pathways at electrode surfaces, compromising cell performance. In this study, we identify a detrimental interaction between succinonitrile (SN) and lithium bis(oxalato)borate (LiBOB) on a graphite-silicon (Gr-Si) anode. Specifically, an electron-deficient boron-embedded solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) derived from LiBOB promotes the reduction of the electron-rich nitrile moieties of SN, disrupting fluoroethylene carbonate (FEC)-driven SEI construction. Based on this mechanism, SN was replaced with triisopropanolamine borate (TPAB), which mitigates transition metal dissolution through its amine moiety while forming a robust borate-based cathode electrolyte interphase. Moreover, TPAB combined with LiBOB avoided detrimental side reductions at the anode–electrolyte interface. The FEC-LiBOB-TPAB combination creates thermally stable interphases on the Gr-Si anode and LiNi0.91Co0.08Al0.01O2 cathode (4.8 mAh cm–2), enabling 68.7% capacity retention after 300 cycles at 45 °C and 1C.

title: Rare diseases are an overlooked dimension in climate–health adaptation
abstract: A resilient society must prepare not only for common harms but also for uncommon vulnerabilities, such as rare disease where the consequences leave no room for failure. Ensuring that people with rare diseases have reliable access to essential care is crucial for fairness and safety in a changing climate.

title: Shear-Driven Structural Ordering Enables High Energy Density in Ferroelectric Polymer Capacitors
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Polymer film capacitors are fundamental to modern power electronics, yet low permittivity restricts their energy density. Although poly(vinylidene fluoride) (PVDF) possesses high intrinsic permittivity, stabilizing its polar structure remains thermodynamically challenging. Here, we report a scalable physical processing strategy to optimize PVDF-based films via a specialized shear-imposed coating methodology. By employing a micro-structured blade, we generate intense local shear flow fields that exert hydrodynamic tension to drive a coil-stretch transition. This process drives an α-to-β phase transition and templates the growth of oriented, polar-phase-rich crystal structures. Furthermore, we develop a stage-wise regulation strategy using binary solvents to orchestrate evaporation dynamics, effectively trapping these metastable shear-induced conformations before relaxation. Effective across the PVDF copolymer family, this method enables P(VDF-HFP) films to achieve a high energy density of 20.05 J/cm3, a 44% improvement over conventional casting. This work provides a general, non-chemical pathway for manufacturing high-performance functional polymers through multi-physical field synergistic regulation.

title: Colloidal ALD Epitaxial Shelling Enhances Stability and Photoluminescence of Blue Perovskite Nanocrystals
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract A modified colloidal atomic layer deposition at room temperature grows a vacancy-ordered Cs2SnCl6 shell epitaxially on CsPbCl3 nanocrystals, avoiding the core degradation and parasitic shell nucleation that accompany high-temperature routes. The resulting core–shell nanocrystals achieve an absolute photoluminescence quantum yield of 62% and retain 65% of their emission after six months of ambient storage and 30% after 48 h of exposure to added water.

title: Electrolyte-Derived Chemical Activation Enables Reversible Cathode Chemistry in Magnesium Batteries
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Rechargeable magnesium (Mg) metal batteries are promising high-energy-density alternatives to lithium-ion systems, yet sluggish cathode kinetics hinder their development. Departing from the conventional host-centric view, we demonstrate that reversibility in Mg batteries can be governed by electrolyte-derived reaction chemistry. Here, we harness trace water to impart controlled electrolyte reactivity, enabling electrolyte-derived Mg/Cl-containing species to participate in cathode activation. In tunnel-type MnO2, the regulated electrolyte induces lattice expansion and improves electrochemical reversibility. In organic cathodes, improved rechargeability is consistent with a stabilizing role of Cl– in anion-coupled redox. Because polar-solvent chemistry can irreversibly passivate Mg metal, a Sn/MgCl2 artificial interface suppresses parasitic anode reactions while preserving cathode activation. This strategy enables reversible electrochemistry across oxide, organic, and conversion cathodes, including α/γ-MnO2, methylphenothiazine, tetrathiafulvalene, and hybrid I2/O2 systems. These findings establish electrolyte-derived chemical activation as a guiding principle for regulating cathode reaction pathways in magnesium batteries.

title: Robust Dipicolinic Acid‐Anchored Self‐Assembled Monolayers for High‐Performance Wide‐Bandgap and Tandem Perovskite Photovoltaics
abstract: ABSTRACT The anchoring group of self‐assembled monolayer (SAM) hole‐transporting materials dictates both substrate binding and interfacial passivation, serving as a key lever for high‐performance perovskite photovoltaics. Herein, we report a novel SAM molecular material, denoted by XS21 , engineered with a multidentate dipicolinic acid (DPA) anchoring core to address conventional adhesion and degradation limitations. From an experimental perspective, the DPA anchor is found to promote molecular chemisorption onto the substrate, potentially originating from the dual‐action mechanism of pyridine–Ni coordination coupled with dicarboxylate‐metal interaction. Furthermore, XS21 imparts both low acid‐dissociation constants ( K a ) and superior ultraviolet (UV) photostability. Consequently, wide‐bandgap (1.79 eV) perovskite solar cells containing XS21 deliver a champion power conversion efficiency (PCE) of 21.54% with an exceptional open‐circuit voltage of 1.372 V. Crucially, integrating XS21 into monolithic all‐perovskite tandem solar cells yields a remarkable PCE of 29.62%, alongside an outstanding operational stability (retaining >90% of initial efficiency after 900 h of continuous operation). This work establishes multi‐dentate pyridine‐carboxylate anchoring as a vital paradigm for next‐generation efficient and stable perovskite photovoltaics.

title: Breaking the Boltzmann Limit: A Review of Emerging Ultralow‐Power Transistor Technologies
abstract: ABSTRACT As complementary metal‐oxide‐semiconductor (CMOS) technology scales down to the sub‐2 nm node, the dramatic surge in power density has emerged as a fundamental bottleneck. Conventional metal‐oxide‐semiconductor field‐effect transistors (MOSFETs) are constrained by the 60 mV/dec Boltzmann thermal limit, rendering further supply voltage reduction exceedingly challenging. To surmount this fundamental limit, various novel sub‐60 mV/dec steep‐switching devices have been proposed, including tunnel field‐effect transistors (TFETs), negative‐capacitance field‐effect transistors (NCFETs), and cold‐source field‐effect transistors (CSFETs). A comprehensive review of the evolution of sub‑60 mV/dec technologies is presented, with particular emphasis on the three mainstream approaches: TFETs, NCFETs, and CSFETs. The underlying physical principles, recent research advances, optimization strategies, and remaining challenges of these devices are thoroughly analyzed. Finally, prospective directions for future breakthroughs are discussed, encompassing novel materials exploration, the synergistic integration of multiple physical mechanisms, and the experimental verification of integration with advanced CMOS nodes.

title: Robust Spin Splitting and Fermiology in the Layered Altermagnet CoNb4Se8
abstract: ABSTRACT Altermagnetism defies conventional classifications of collinear magnetic phases, combining compensated magnetization with momentum‐dependent, nonrelativistic spin splitting. While altermagnetic band splitting has been established in three‐dimensional compounds such as MnTe and CrSb, layered altermagnets remain far less explored spectroscopically. Here, combining termination‐resolved micro‐ARPES, fine photon‐energy mapping, spin‐ARPES, and density functional theory, we map the three‐dimensional fermiology of the layered g ‐wave altermagnet , obtained by ordered Co intercalation of 2H‐. We resolve the spin–split branches of the altermagnetic pairs directly in the raw photoemission spectra and, with spin‐ARPES at these experimentally identified momenta, show the reversal of the spin polarization at opposite momenta and between two regions of the sample, consistent with opposite time‐reversal domains, and its absence along the symmetry‐protected nodal –K direction. We further report a weak low‐temperature anomaly near T 0 ≈ 50–60 K, detected by magnetometry, temperature‐dependent micro‐ARPES, and ultrafast reflectivity, whose microscopic origin remains open. These results provide a momentum‐resolved benchmark of the electronic structure of a layered altermagnet.

title: Disentangling Polaron Formation Pathways in Y6 by Probing Noninteracting and Interacting Chromophores via Transient Absorption Spectroscopy
abstract: ABSTRACT In highly efficient organic solar cells, the optoelectronic properties of the non‐fullerene acceptor Y6 are governed by the molecular packing of noninteracting and interacting molecules. In this study, steady‐state and transient absorption spectroscopy are employed to disentangle the spectral signatures and excited‐state dynamics of interacting and noninteracting Y6 in solution and thin films. By controlling aggregation in dilute solution, we identify localized Frenkel‐type excitons (LE) on noninteracting Y6 and aggregate excitons (AE) on intermolecular interacting Y6. The AEs exhibit strongly fluence‐dependent lifetimes (30–200 ps) governed by singlet–singlet annihilation, whereas localized excitons decay monoexponentially on a nanosecond timescale. Furthermore, long‐lived polaronic states are observed to form on aggregated Y6 within tens of picoseconds and persist into the nanosecond regime. Comparison with thin‐film measurements reveals similar processes with an additional ultrafast energy transfer from noninteracting chromophores to aggregated domains. These results establish a consistent framework for assigning transient absorption features in Y6 and suggest that, in neat films of Y6, the pairwise formation of polarons arises from an Onsager‐like autoionization process of delocalized excitons in domains of interacting Y6 with moderate yield. This provides central insight into charge‐generation mechanisms in Y6‐based photovoltaic systems.

title: Durable Interphase Incorporating Cross‐Linked Polymer Enables Long‐Calendar‐Life Lithium Metal Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT The practical deployment of lithium (Li) metal batteries is hindered by not only cycle life but also calendar life. The poor calendar life stems from both the repeated reconstruction of the solid‐electrolyte interphase (SEI) during cycles and, particularly, the continuous growth of SEI during storage. Herein, a durable SEI with high mechanical stability against volume fluctuations and superior passivation capability to suppress electrolyte permeation is demonstrated by integrating inorganics and a cross‐linked polymer into the SEI. Concretely, a cross‐linked polymer with high modulus and low swelling is in‐situ incorporated among the inorganics of an anion‐derived SEI. The elastic modulus of the SEI is significantly increased from 1.63 to 4.37 GPa, and the compactness of the SEI is also improved to suppress electrolyte permeation. Consequently, the cycle life and calendar life of Li metal coin cells are extended by 73% (from 190 to 329 cycles) and 129% (from 1553 to 3561 h), respectively. Furthermore, a prototype pouch cell (506 Wh kg −1 ) undergoes 124 cycles. This work establishes an effective strategy that concurrently improves the mechanical and passivation performance of the SEI, tackling the critical challenge of calendar life in Li metal batteries.

title: A Simple Descriptor for Solid‐State Ionic Conductors Across Chemistries
abstract: ABSTRACT The discovery of new solid‐state ionic conductors remains challenging because ion transport depends sensitively on both mobile‐ion chemistry and the host crystal framework. Although atomistic calculations can evaluate migration barriers directly, simple descriptors can greatly facilitate screening large materials spaces and gaining mechanistic insight. However, existing descriptors often show limited transferability across mobile‐ion chemistries and material classes. Here, we generate a diverse dataset of ion‐migration barriers spanning Li‐, Na‐, K‐, and Mg‐ion conductors across oxides, sulfides, and halides, and use it to systematically benchmark descriptors. From this analysis, we devise distance contraction, ∆ d , a simple local geometric descriptor that measures the largest contraction of mobile‐ion–neighbor distances relative to their equilibrium values along a migration pathway. This quantity captures the dominant short‐range repulsion penalty associated with ion migration and consistently distinguishes low‐ from high‐barrier pathways across chemistries. Using ∆ d in a high‐throughput screening workflow, we recover many known fast‐ion conductors and identify previously unexplored candidates, with fast‐ion transport validated by nudged elastic band calculations and ab initio molecular dynamics simulations. Beyond screening, ∆ d links diverse ion‐transport mechanisms to a common physical quantity: The largest distance contraction experienced by the migrating ion.

title: Chiral Phonon–Driven Ultrafast Spin Currents in a Non‐Magnetic Ferroelectric
abstract: ABSTRACT The discovery that fundamental lattice vibrations can carry angular momentum allows non‐magnetic materials to exhibit properties that until now have only been observable in magnetic materials. However, the role of these specific vibrations, commonly known as chiral phonons, in driving ultrafast spin dynamics has not yet been explored experimentally. Here, using broadband terahertz emission spectroscopy, we demonstrate that the non‐magnetic ferroelectric generates signals consistent with a ultrafast spin current after excitation with an ultrafast laser pulse, which we attribute to a chiral phonon–induced spin Seebeck effect. We suggest that the transient heating creates an non‐equilibrium phonon distribution, resulting in a net angular momentum and magnetization perpendicular to the thermal gradient, which is converted into a terahertz electromagnetic pulse via an inverse spin‐Hall effect in a thin metal overlayer. The emitted field reverses sign upon flipping the sample orientation or replacing Pt with W, consistent with spin‐current generation. Polarization‐resolved measurements reveal controllable terahertz ellipticity, indicating an additional polarization‐dependent ultrafast response. Our results establish chiral phonons as a route for generating ultrafast spin currents in non‐magnetic materials as well as providing a pathway toward terahertz sources with switchable handedness.

title: Emerging Lipid Nanoparticle Targeting Strategies for Extrahepatic Delivery of RNA Therapeutics
abstract: ABSTRACT Lipid nanoparticles (LNPs) have transformed RNA therapeutics through their high delivery efficiency, scalable manufacturing, and favorable safety profiles, as demonstrated by COVID‐19 mRNA vaccines and clinically approved small interfering RNA (siRNA) therapeutics. However, extending RNA delivery beyond the liver to extrahepatic tissues, including the spleen, lungs, lymph nodes, brain, and tumors, remains challenging because of the intrinsic hepatotropism of conventional LNPs and their limited cell‐type specificity. Recent advances in lipid chemistry, particle engineering, surface functionalization, protein corona modulation, and route‐specific administration have enabled new strategies to redirect LNPs toward specific tissues and cell populations. This review systematically examines these approaches and highlights key determinants of LNP tropism, including formulation composition, surface properties, endogenous protein adsorption, and administration route. We further discuss the clinical translation of extrahepatic LNP delivery, covering clinically validated products, emerging therapeutic candidates, and gaps between preclinical models and human applications. Major challenges include cell‐resolved biodistribution, long‐term safety, repeated‐dose immunogenicity, cross‐study comparability, and standardized quantitative assessment. Finally, we explore how high‐throughput screening, machine learning, and data‐driven design can accelerate the rational optimization of next‐generation LNPs. These advances may facilitate precise tissue‐ and cell‐selective RNA delivery, expanding the therapeutic potential of RNA medicines beyond the liver.

title: Dual Single Atoms Boosting Photocatalytic Upcycling of Raw Polyvinylidene Fluoride Plastic
abstract: ABSTRACT Polyvinylidene fluoride (PVDF) is a highly recalcitrant fluorinated polymer that is highly resistant to chemical degradation, making its sustainable recycling and upcycling challenging. Despite its widespread use as a binder in the lithium‐ion battery industry, effective strategies for converting PVDF waste into value‐added chemicals remain limited. To resolve this, Fe and Cu dual single atoms incorporated on a new two‐dimensional material nanosheets (In 2 P 3 S 9 NSs/Fe‐Cu DSAs) were prepared as photocatalysts for direct raw PVDF plastic conversion to high‐value chemicals. The best‐performing photocatalyst (Fe 1.0 Cu 0.5 ) achieves a total acetic/formic acid generation of ∼1351.8 µmol g −1 . Various in situ characterizations such as atomic force microscopy‐kelvin probe force microscopy, x‐ray photoelectron spectroscopy, and electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) demonstrate superior electron extraction from In 2 P 3 S 9 NSs to Fe and Cu DSAs, after which the electrons are subsequently scavenged by O 2 under ambient conditions. Moreover, quenching experiments as well as in situ infrared spectroscopy, and in situ EPR reveal the vital impact of photoexcited electrons and hydroxyl radicals in PVDF upcycling into high‐value products. These findings highlight the significant potential of photocatalysis in transforming one of the most resistant plastic wastes (PVDF) into value‐added products, providing a sustainable remedy for plastic pollution crisis.

title: Biomimetic Dichalcogenide‐Hybrid Nanozymes With Glutathione Peroxidase‐Like Activity for Liver Protection
abstract: ABSTRACT Glutathione peroxidase (GPX)‐mimetic nanozymes are a promising strategy to restore redox homeostasis, but many existing systems rely on metals and remain limited by cytotoxicity, poor selectivity, and susceptibility to catalytic deactivation. Inspired by the active‐site chemistry of native GPX, we designed dichalcogenide‐hybrid mesoporous silica nanoparticles (MSNs) as inorganic–organic nanozymes with tunable sulfur and selenium environments. Structure–activity analysis showed that GPX‐like performance is governed by chalcogen composition, chalcogen density, and spatial proximity of S/Se within the framework, which together regulate reversible disulfide/diselenide redox cycling and substrate access. Among the materials tested, the diselenide–hybrid framework exhibited the highest activity, with improved selectivity and biocompatibility relative to the disulfide‐hybrid analogue, and conventional metal‐based GPX mimics. Mechanistic studies indicated efficient glutathione‐dependent detoxification of peroxides and lipid peroxides through catalytically active chalcogen intermediates. In vivo, the optimized diselenide‐hybrid material protected against acetaminophen‐induced and rifampicin‐induced liver injury, reduced oxidative stress and inflammation, restored antioxidant capacity, and improved survival. It also alleviated steatosis and metabolic dysfunction in metabolic dysfunction‐associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) models. These findings establish dichalcogenide–hybrid frameworks as effective GPX‐like nanozymes and a promising platform for the treatment of oxidative stress‐associated liver diseases.

title: Synchronic Multilevel Assembly Toward Mesoporous Nanosized Intercalation‐Type Framework Anodes for Fast‐Charging Sodium‐Ion Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Intercalation‐type metal oxides are promising anodes for fast‐charging sodium‐ion batteries (SIBs). However, viable electrode candidates remain scarce, constituting a major bottleneck and motivating intensive research into diverse structural frameworks. Here, we report a synchronic multilevel assembly strategy for synthesizing mesoporous intercalation‐type metal oxide framework anodes. Atomic‐scale assembly of cations, combined with in situ formation of conductive carbon networks, enables the synthesis of structurally tunable nanosized sodium titanate and overcomes the challenges of preparing multimetal oxide nanocrystals under high temperatures. The M‐Na 4 Ti 5 O 12 /C composite delivers superior rate capability (∼115 mAh g −1 at 10 A g −1 ) and cycling stability (−1 ) for sodium storage. Its outstanding kinetics arise from ultrafast Na + diffusion through interconnected mesoporous channels and low‐barrier, nanoscale ion‐conduction pathways. A pouch cell delivers a power density of ∼4.7 kW kg −1 and cycles stably for 1200 cycles, outperforming hard carbon at high rates. This work establishes a rational design framework for developing high‐rate battery materials.

title: Robust Sodium–Metal Batteries Through Electrolyte‐Mediated Interfacial Regulation: Fundamentals, Design Strategies, and Operando Characterization
abstract: ABSTRACT Sodium–metal batteries (SMBs) exhibit high theoretical specific capacity and take advantage of sodium's natural abundance and low cost, showing great promise for broad next‐generation energy‐storage applications. In this review, we summarize the major practical bottlenecks restricting SMB development. The solid–electrolyte interphase (SEI) serves as a key mediator to overcome these challenges, and its formation mechanisms are systematically outlined. We comprehensively review diverse electrolyte strategies, including solvent engineering, salt chemistry optimization, additive utilization, high‐concentration, localized high‐concentration, and weakly solvating electrolytes, for modulating Na + transport and generating mechanically robust, ion‐conductive yet electronically insulating SEI layers. We further discuss advanced in‐situ/operando characterizations combined with multiscale computational modeling and machine‐learning techniques as powerful tools to decipher the dynamic evolution of sodium–metal interfaces. Particular focus is placed on the coupled effects of current density, temperature, electrolyte composition, interfacial layers on sodium nucleation, dendrite growth, dead‐sodium formation, and Coulombic efficiency (CE). Finally, future directions for SEI engineering have been outlook toward high‐performance, practical sodium–metal batteries.

title: Healable Thermoset Elastomeric Materials for Passive Radiative Cooling
abstract: ABSTRACT Passive radiative cooling (PRC) technology with zero‐energy uptake is an efficient thermal management strategy for the development of sustainable society. Fabrication of PRC materials with intrinsic extensibility/dimensional stability and efficient healability that can adapt to irregular shapes with prolonged lifetime remains a significant challenge. The present study introduces a design principle for mechanically robust and healable PRC films based on a cross‐linked elastomeric network with combined physical interactions and dynamic covalent bonds, which can be readily modulated by inorganic coating and micro‐/nano‐porous hierarchical architectures while retaining extensibility and healability. Such thermosetting elastomeric PRC films are scalable with strong solar reflectance and long‐wave infrared emittance, realizing excellent cooling performance even after physical damage and healing process. It demonstrates excellent roof cooling ability in summer yet efficient ice‐sculpture preservation function in winter. The scalable synthesis of thermoset elastomeric PRC films opens up new pathways to realize flexible, stable and healable PRC materials, highly promising for practical applications.

title: Manipulating Hofmeister Effect for Fabricating Freestanding Ionic Covalent Organic Framework Membranes
abstract: ABSTRACT Interfacial assembly of ionic covalent organic framework (iCOF) membranes remains a significant challenge. In this study, we report the fabrication of freestanding iCOF membranes by manipulating Hofmeister effect during interfacial polymerization (IP) process. Different kinds of inorganic salts are introduced into the aqueous phase to regulate the dissolution and crystallization dynamics of TpPa‐SO 3 H. We discover that Li 2 SO 4 provides the optimal ion‐specific regulation by combining a strongly hydrated anion that effectively dehydrates the growing iCOF and a cation that interacts only weakly with the sulfonate framework, enabling TpPa‐SO 3 H to enrich and stay at the interface. This ion‐specific synergy facilitates the subsequent π–π stacking and ordered assembly into highly crystalline, intact freestanding membranes. The resulting membrane demonstrates a high proton conductivity of 334.7 mS cm −1 at 100°C and 98% RH.

title: Unstabilized Alkyl Radicals in Photochemistry: From Emerging Precursors to Reactivity
abstract: ABSTRACT Carbon‐centered radicals have progressively become indispensable tools in modern synthetic chemistry. Visible‐light photochemistry has emerged as a powerful platform for organic transformations, enabling the selective generation of radical species under remarkably mild and sustainable conditions. The controlled generation of unstabilized alkyl radicals, however, remains one of the most challenging and rapidly evolving frontiers in the field. In recent years, substantial efforts have been devoted to the development of novel radical precursors specifically designed to enable the efficient formation of these highly valuable intermediates under photoinduced conditions. This Minireview highlights recent advances in the design of unstabilized carbon‐centered radical precursors, systematically categorizing them according to their structural features. Particular attention is devoted to understanding how precursor design influences redox properties, bond fragmentation pathways, and so forth with the aim of laying the groundwork for the future design of increasingly efficient radical precursors and the discovery of new photochemical reactivity paradigms.

title: Tunable Spin‐Polarized Chiral Plasmonic Films for Dual‐Mode Enantiomer Recognition
abstract: ABSTRACT Chirality‐induced spin selectivity (CISS) has emerged as a frontier research direction in chiral recognition. However, existing CISS‐based sensing platforms are often constrained by structural disorder, limited spin selectivity, and insufficient electrical conductivity, which restrict their practical application in high‐performance chiral sensing. Inspired by the coherent potential fields generated through the hierarchical and ordered assembly of biomacromolecules, which enable efficient long‐range spin transport, we constructed chiral gold superlattice nanofilms (CANFs) through the precise self‐assembly of chiral gold nanoparticles. The CANFs achieved a spin polarization efficiency of up to +94.17% ± 3.72%. Benefiting from their excellent electrical conductivity and spatial‐confinement‐enhanced signal amplification, the CANFs enable dual‐mode enantioselective recognition of kynurenine enantiomers, with a photo‐driven ionic‐current discrimination ratio as high as 10.3. The platform further exhibits outstanding analytical performance, including low limits of detection of 0.024 nM in the photo‐driven mode and 0.012 µM in the electrochemical mode, broad linear response ranges, and good applicability in complex clinical matrices. By integrating CISS‐mediated spin‐polarized transport with nanoconfinement‐enhanced signal transduction, this work establishes a versatile strategy for developing next‐generation real time, high‐performance chiral sensing platforms.

title: Modulation of 9,12‐Substituted o ‐Carboranes Toward Anti‐Kasha Triple‐Fluorescence
abstract: ABSTRACT Achieving triple‐fluorescence from a pure organic compound in solution is nearly impossible, as Kasha's rule only allows single fluorescence from the lowest excited state. In this paper, pyrene‐substituted o ‐carboranes, 1a ‐ c , and 2a , were synthesized within 3–5 steps from commercially available chemicals, and their chemical structures have been confirmed by 1 H NMR, 13 C NMR, and HRMS. The photophysical properties of these compounds have been studied in detail by UV–vis, steady and transient state fluorescence, temperature‐dependent fluorescence, and femtosecond transient absorption spectroscopy, as well as TD‐DFT calculations. The results show that while 2a exhibits only local emission, the B,B‐dipyrenyl‐ o ‐carborane, 1a , shows dual‐emission from locally excited and intramolecular excimer states. Triple‐fluorescence is achieved for 1b and 1c by introducing a small π‐substituent at the carborane carbon vertices, which allows the formation of a charge‐transfer state that is fluorescent in the near‐infrared (NIR) region tailing to 1200 nm. This work provides a new strategy to activate triple‐fluorescence from a single‐component organic compound, opening a new avenue toward multichannel photonic materials and NIR‑II bioimaging.

title: Closed Pores as Internal Stress‐Regulation Units for Practical Silicon–Carbon Anodes
abstract: ABSTRACT Silicon–carbon anodes are among the most promising candidates for high‐energy lithium‐ion batteries, yet their practical implementation remains constrained by lithiation‐induced outward deformation, electrode cracking, and persistent interphase degradation. Here, closed pores are introduced as internal stress‐regulation units to address the coupled mechanical and electrochemical instability of silicon–carbon anodes. Heteroatom‐doped carbon hosts are engineered to contain abundant closed nanopores, which redirect expansion‐induced stress toward the particle interior and suppress macroscopic electrode swelling. Meanwhile, heteroatom doping enlarges the carbon interlayer spacing and enhances electronic conductivity, enabling accelerated and more balanced Li + insertion/extraction kinetics. As a representative material, the nitrogen–doped silicon–carbon composite delivers a reversible capacity of 1756.5 mAh g − 1 , an initial Coulombic efficiency of 90.2%, and 868.4 mAh g −1 at 3 C, while reducing electrode thickness expansion from 38.4% to 13.1% after 50 cycles. The material is further produced in 6 kg batches and enables 2 Ah LiNi 0.8 Co 0.1 Mn 0.1 O 2 (NCM811) pouch cells with 80.0% capacity retention after 1200 cycles and only 8.4% thickness growth after 900 cycles. Machine–learning–guided phosphorus doping further validates the transferability of the closed‐pore design. This work establishes closed‐pore stress regulation as a scalable structural strategy for practical low‐expansion silicon–carbon anodes.

title: Reconstruction of the Electric Double Layer for Long‐Lasting Aqueous Manganese Metal Batteries
abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous Mn metal batteries (AMMBs) have emerged as promising candidates for stationary energy storage owing to the natural abundance of Mn, their operational safety, and their high energy density. However, the high chemical reactivity of the Mn metal anode induces a severe hydrogen evolution reaction (HER), resulting in poor cycling reversibility. Fundamentally, HER is a parasitic cathodic reaction competing with Mn electrodeposition and may accompany Mn corrosion. Its kinetics are influenced by the interfacial water environment within the electric double layer (EDL). In this study, we propose a strategy for reconstructing the EDL by adding n ‐decyltrimethylammonium bromide (10‐DTAB), a surfactant with a relatively high lowest unoccupied molecular orbital (LUMO), to the electrolyte to stabilize the Mn anode. The high LUMO energy level enhances its reduction stability, thus preventing continuous decomposition during cycling and enabling sustained interfacial protection. Consequently, the Mn anode exhibits a markedly enhanced Coulombic efficiency of 93%. This study demonstrates a durable EDL regulation paradigm based on high‐LUMO additives, offering new insights into stabilizing Mn metal anodes and advancing AMMBs toward practical applications.

title: Decoupled Biomass Electrooxidation Over E‐Waste‐Derived Au Enables Low‐Voltage H 2 and Scalable FDCA Production
abstract: ABSTRACT The oxygen evolution reaction (OER) constitutes a major energetic bottleneck in electrochemical hydrogen production. Replacing OER with low‐potential organic oxidation provides an effective route to reduce cell voltage while enabling value‐added chemical synthesis. Here, a nanostructured Au electrocatalyst is developed from recycled electronic waste via a corrosion‐template–assisted electrodeposition strategy. Co(OH) 2 nanoarrays grown on nickel foam act as a sacrificial template to regulate galvanic displacement between chloride‐coordinated Au(III) species and metallic Ni, inducing polycrystalline Au nucleation with tailored surface structures. Subsequent electrodeposition precisely controls Au size and dispersion, resulting in a substantially enlarged electrochemically active surface area. In alkaline media, the Au electrode selectively drives aldehyde oxidation of 5‐hydroxymethylfurfural to 5‐hydroxymethyl‐2‐furoic acid at potentials well below those required for OER, while enabling concurrent anodic hydrogen evolution and stable low‐voltage bipolar hydrogen production. In a flow‐electrolysis configuration, current densities of ∼0.6 A cm −2 are sustained at a low cell voltage of ∼1.2 V for over 200 h. By decoupling low‐potential aldehyde oxidation from high‐potential deep oxidation in a tandem electrolyzer, stepwise electrochemical upgrading from HMF to FDCA is achieved with reduced overall energy input. This work establishes a scalable electrochemical platform that integrates low‐voltage hydrogen production with high‐value biomass conversion.

title: Vitamin C‐Induced Photo‐Redox Threshold Enables High‐Fidelity Volumetric Printing of Collagen
abstract: ABSTRACT Tomographic volumetric printing (TVP) enables rapid fabrication of complex, centimeter‐scale 3D architectures. TVP of native proteins such as collagen is attractive because it preserves native bioactive motifs that regulate cell–matrix signaling. However, direct TVP of collagen remains challenging because dityrosine crosslinking, driven by visible‐light‐activated Ru(II)bpy 3 2+ /sodium persulfate (SPS), lacks an effective inhibitory mechanism. This results in near‐immediate crosslinking upon light exposure, leading to an insufficient nonlinear threshold response that fails to suppress background curing. Here, we introduce vitamin C (L‐ascorbic acid) as a biocompatible redox regulator to overcome this limitation. We demonstrated that vitamin C established a photo‐redox threshold by suppressing Ru(III) accumulation and scavenging persulfate radicals within the Ru/SPS system, thereby delaying dityrosine crosslinking until vitamin C depletion. This threshold generated the nonlinear response required for TVP, enabling high‐fidelity volumetric printing of collagen. Post‐printing construct densification (∼53% shrinkage) further improved feature resolution (80 µm positive; 120 µm negative) and yielded mechanically stable and highly stretchable hydrogels (up to 180% strain). Collagen resin with vitamin C supported both cell seeding post‐printing and cell‐laden printing with high cell density and viability, enabling the rapid biofabrication of cell‐instructive 3D microenvironments.

title: Hyperbranched Epoxy Topology Enables Covalent Interphases and Penetration‐Locking Thermoset Networks
abstract: ABSTRACT The inherent trade‐off between high mechanical performance and recyclability in carbon fiber‐reinforced epoxy composites (CFREs) remains a fundamental challenge in epoxy resin design. Herein, we introduce a topology engineering strategy based on an imide‐containing dual‐role hyperbranched platform, which acts simultaneously as reactive tougheners and interfacial coupling agents. Within the matrix, the hyperbranched architecture interpenetrates the linear epoxy network, forming a distinctive dual‐phase “penetration‐locking” topology that reduces free volume and increases effective cross‐link density. At the fiber‐matrix interface, thiol‐terminated hyperbranched molecules enable covalent interphase formation via thiol‐ene click chemistry, enhancing interfacial adhesion and stress transfer. This chemically integrated design enables cost‐effective T300‐based composites to reach a tensile strength of 740 MPa, comparable to conventional T800‐based composites, while T800‐based composites achieve up to 1.1 GPa. Importantly, the incorporation of imide and ester linkages introduces chemically addressable cleavage sites, enabling selective depolymerization under mild alkaline methanolysis, recovery of carbon fibers with retained integrity, and upcycling of oligomeric products as curing agents. This work establishes a molecular design framework that couples network topology, interfacial chemistry, and dynamic covalent functionality, providing a versatile platform for high‐performance thermoset composites with improved lifecycle sustainability.

title: Potassium‐Concentration‐Gated C–N Coupling Enables a Volcano‐Shaped Selectivity Window for Electrocatalytic Urea Synthesis
abstract: ABSTRACT Alkali metal cations influence electrochemical interfaces, but their role in regulating urea electrosynthesis remains incompletely understood. Here, we combine constant‐potential ab initio molecular dynamics (AIMD), classical molecular dynamics (cMD), flow‐cell electrolysis, and in situ infrared spectroscopy to investigate how cations affect urea formation from CO 2 and nitrate on Cu. Among Li + , Na + , K + , and Cs + , K + affords the lowest calculated barrier for direct *CO–*NO coupling and the highest measured urea Faradaic efficiency. Varying the K + concentration reveals a volcano‐shaped dependence of urea activity and selectivity, with a maximum at a partial current density of 13.62 mA cm −2 and Faradaic efficiency of 24.50% near 1.20 M K + . AIMD calculations identify a minimum coupling barrier at an intermediate nominal K + concentration and elucidate how K + concentration regulates precursor geometry and charge redistribution. Complementary cMD simulations reveal concentration‐dependent changes in interfacial reactant distributions and water structure, with infrared spectral features providing experimental evidence of changes in interfacial reaction chemistry. Together, these results establish an optimal K + concentration window governed by the coupled roles of elementary‐step kinetics and electrolyte organization in urea electrosynthesis.

title: Synergistic High‐Entropy and Anchoring Stabilization of PtPdIrRuCu Alloy Nanoparticles on N, O‐Doped Carbon Cage Fibers for Durable and Selective PET Upcycling
abstract: ABSTRACT High‐entropy alloy nanoparticles (HEA NPs) are promising electrocatalysts, yet their ultrasmall size makes them vulnerable to migration‐induced coalescence (MIC), a sintering pathway that intrinsic high‐entropy effects cannot suppress. Herein, we anchor ultrasmall PtPdIrRuCu HEA NPs on N, O‐doped carbon cage fibers (NOCCFs). The N/O anchoring sites inhibit MIC through strong metal–support interactions, which, together with the intrinsic resistance of HEA to Ostwald ripening, synergistically suppress sintering. After 700 °C annealing, the PtPdIrRuCu NPs size increases from 2.8 nm to only 3.8 nm, whereas Pt/C aggregates from 2.3 nm to 21.8 nm. In ethylene glycol oxidation reaction (EGOR), the PtPdIrRuCu/NOCCFs delivers a mass activity of 7.66 A·mg Pt − 1 (7.3‑fold that of Pt/C) and a Faradaic efficiency of 95.8% toward glycolic acid (GA). A membrane electrode assembly (MEA) flow electrolyzer runs stably over 240 h with >90% GA selectivity. Mechanistic studies reveal that the PtPdIrRuCu/NOCCFs enhances *OH adsorption to promote the GA pathway, accelerates CO ads oxidation via oxophilic Ir/Ru sites to prevent catalyst poisoning, and elevates both C–C cleavage and overoxidation barriers to suppress byproducts.

title: Organocatalytic Dynamic Kinetic Resolution for the Stereoconvergent Synthesis of N–N Axially Chiral Compounds
abstract: ABSTRACT Dynamic kinetic resolution (DKR) serves as a fundamental approach in asymmetric synthesis which enables the efficient conversion of racemic starting materials into a single stereoisomer, yet its extension to racemic diastereomers remains a formidable challenge, and reported DKR processes have largely been restricted to substrates bearing a single stereogenic element. Herein, we report an organocatalytic DKR with catalyst‐accelerated racemization and epimerization for the asymmetric construction of significant N–N axially chiral compounds through the merger of a reversible Pudovik addition with an irreversible, stereoselective phospha ‐Brook rearrangement. Under bioinspired peptide‐phosphonium salt catalysis, a wide range of N–N axially chiral products were obtained in good yields and high enantioselectivities. Scale‐up synthesis and product derivatization further underscore the synthetic utility of this protocol. Mechanistic studies support a DKR process involving reversible racemization and epimerization through prochiral intermediates, identify the phospha ‐Brook rearrangement as the stereodetermining step, and reveal key roles of hydrogen‐bonding and ion‐pairing interactions in catalyst‐controlled stereochemical induction. This work establishes a new paradigm for the catalytic asymmetric synthesis of axially chiral molecules.

title: Downsizing Electrophilic MAX‐Derived Helical Zipper Peptides to Covalently Bind and Degrade Oncogenic MYC
abstract: ABSTRACT MYC is an intrinsically disordered oncoprotein that drives cancer progression via widespread transcriptional dysregulation. Upon binding partner protein MAX, their basic‐helix1‐loop‐helix2‐Zip (bHLH‐Zip) domains assemble into an ordered heterodimer that binds E‐box DNA to promote cellular proliferation. This interface has been undruggable by small molecules. Here, we report a novel covalent downsizing strategy to inhibit MYC‐MAX interaction by targeting the C‐terminal Cys438 present in MYC, but absent in MAX and related proteins. Incorporating a mild acrylamide electrophile to covalently bond specifically with Cys438 enabled truncation of MAX to shorter peptides with high affinity for MYC. Using intracellular protein‐fragment complementation, MAX‐derived sequences were optimized for interaction with MYC. Further downsizing, inserting a helix‐inducing constraint, and optimal electrophile positioning produced a serum‐stable 24‐residue covalent inhibitor that captured endogenous MYC from cell lysates. Esterifying six Glu/Asp residues enhanced membrane permeability, while intracellular esterolysis achieved robust cytosolic and nuclear accumulation of the MYC inhibitor. Microscopy confirmed nuclear delivery correlating directly with progressive loss of nuclear MYC. The esterified compound exhibited antiproliferative activity across MYC‐dependent cancer cell lines, inhibited migration, and triggered ubiquitin‐proteasome mediated MYC degradation, downregulating key target genes downstream of MYC. This covalent downsizing approach is a generalizable chemical strategy for targeting recalcitrant transcription factors.

title: Visible‐Light‐Induced Radical Carbonylative Dearomatization of Unactivated Indoles
abstract: ABSTRACT Dearomative hydrofunctionalization of indoles represents an appealing strategy to access C(sp 3 )‐rich indoline scaffolds for drug discovery; however, such transformations typically require activated substrates, leaving unactivated indoles largely unexplored. Herein, we report a photochemical radical carbonylative dearomatization of unactivated indoles under visible light irradiation. Central to this protocol is the interception of the highly reactive indolenium intermediate—generated in situ via acid‐mediated C3‐protonation—through the formation of an electron donor−acceptor (EDA) complex with 4‐alkyl‐1,4‐dihydropyridines (DHPs). This photoactive EDA complex initiates a mechanistically distinct radical pathway that effectively circumvents the detrimental dimerization typically plaguing indolenium intermediates. Subsequent radical carbonylation and radical cross‐coupling enable the carbonylative dearomatization of a broad range of indoles with diverse alkyl‐DHPs. The method exhibits excellent functional group tolerance and broad substrate scope, furnishing various 2‐acylindolines in generally good yields. Comprehensive mechanistic studies, including control experiments, electron paramagnetic resonance spectroscopy, and UV/vis absorption analyses, support a radical‐radical coupling mechanism as the key step in this transformation.

title: Molecular Preorganization Unlocks Reversible Solid‐State Photoconversion in Dianthrylnaphthalene‐Based Molecular Solar Thermal Systems
abstract: ABSTRACT Molecular solar thermal (MOST) systems capable of harnessing sunlight, storing it as chemical energy in the form of a photoisomer, and releasing it as thermal energy on demand represent a promising strategy for renewable solar energy utilization both in liquid‐based devices and the solid state. However, the implementation of MOST materials in the solid state is limited by restricted molecular motion in the condensed phase, which hampers the geometrical requirements for photoisomerization, as well as by inner filter effects which can prevent quantitative photoconversion or necessitate long irradiation times. To address these challenges, three dianthrylnaphthalenes were designed to pre‐organize two anthracene moieties in a face‐to‐face geometry favorable for intramolecular photodimerization. This molecular design increased the forward photoisomerization quantum yield compared to ortho ‐dianthrylbenzenes, reaching 32%, while enabling solid‐state switching. In particular, the acenaphthene‐linked derivative underwent quantitative conversion to its higher‐energy photoisomer in both thin films and bulk crystalline powders. Electron diffraction analysis revealed elongated newly formed C─C bonds in the photoisomer, with refined lengths of 1.81(2) and 1.63(2) Å, exceeding the generally observed length of a C sp3 ─C sp3 bond. These results demonstrate how molecular preorganization can overcome limitations of anthracene‐based MOST systems and expand their potential for solid‐state solar energy storage applications.

title: Cascade Electrosynthesis of Aryl Imides and Sulfonimides From N 2 via Integrated Nitrogen Fixation and C─N/S─N Bond Formation
abstract: ABSTRACT Direct synthesis of organonitrogen compounds from dinitrogen (N 2 ) remains a formidable challenge because N 2 ‐to‐C─N bond formation requires nitrogen fixation to be coupled with selective functionalization of N 2 ‐derived intermediates before their termination as ammonia. Herein, we report a cascade electrochemical strategy that converts N 2 into aryl imides and aryl sulfonimides in a gas‐diffusion electrochemical flow cell. Under proton‐donor‐free conditions, electrochemically generated Li 3 N is intercepted by acyl or sulfonyl chlorides, enabling one‐pot synthesis of aryl imides and sulfonimides from N 2 in yields up to 57%. This represents a notably high yield for direct N 2 ‐derived organonitrogen synthesis. This work couples N 2 fixation and C─N/S─N bond formation, expanding electrochemical nitrogen fixation beyond ammonia synthesis toward direct construction of value‐added C─N/S─N bonds.

title: Boosting N , N ‐Dimethylformamide Electrosynthesis via a Surface Active Additive
abstract: ABSTRACT Electrosynthesis of N , N ‐dimethylformamide (DMF) via C─N coupling offers a sustainable alternative to energy‐intensive thermal routes but is hindered by low reactant concentration at the anode and sluggish proton‐coupled electron transfer. Here we report a new electrochemical route for DMF synthesis by the co‐oxidation of dimethylamine and ethylene glycol. Notably, over a CuO electrode, the addition of 0.5 mM sodium dodecylbenzenesulfonate (SDBS) to the electrolyte significantly enhances reaction kinetics and Faradaic efficiency for DMF (FE DMF ), achieving a DMF production rate to 0.78 mmol h −1 cm −2 , over three times higher than that without SDBS. Using a 25 cm 2 CuO electrode in 0.5 M NaHCO 3 with 0.5 mM SDBS, a current of approximately 2.0 A and a DMF production rate of 7.5 mmol h −1 are achieved. Mechanistic investigations reveal that SDBS acts as a multifunctional ionic anchor, reorienting its sulfonate group toward the anode and projecting its hydrophobic tail into the electrolyte under reaction conditions. This configuration suppresses the oxygen evolution reaction while simultaneously enriching reactants, promoting deprotonation and proton transfer, and facilitating electron transfer, thereby enhancing both reaction kinetics and FE DMF .

title: Hydrated Electron‐Activated Nano‐Radiosensitizer Induces Sustained Endoplasmic Reticulum Stress for Potent Tumor Radiosensitization
abstract: ABSTRACT Radiotherapy (RT) efficacy is often limited by two key challenges: rapid restoration of tumor genomic integrity through DNA repair and the lack of tumor‐confined radiosensitization. Although existing radiosensitizers can enhance initial DNA damage, they generally fail to suppress subsequent self‐repair of tumor cells and often induce off‐target toxicity due to nonspecific activation. Here, we report a hydrated electron ()‐activated nano‐radiosensitizer (RT‐nRS) that enables tumor‐confined radiosensitization by converting transient RT‐induced damage into persistent subcellular dysfunction. Unlike conventional RT‐responsive systems that rely on short‐lived reactive oxygen species, RT‐nRS leverages the longer lifetime of to trigger the irradiation‐induced zwitterion‐to‐cationic surface transformation, thereby maintaining systemic circulation stability while enhancing tumor cellular internalization. Furthermore, preferential accumulation and prolonged retention within the endoplasmic reticulum (ER) enable RT‐nRS to induce sustained ER stress, thereby simultaneously amplifying DNA damage and suppressing DNA repair. Our results demonstrate that RT‐nRS effectively overcomes tumor radioresistance while minimizing off‐target toxicity to non‐irradiated normal tissues, leading to significantly enhanced radiotherapy efficacy. Our work establishes hydrated electron‐responsive chemistry as a strategy for spatiotemporally controlled radiosensitization and provides a general framework for converting transient radiotherapeutic stimuli into durable biological outcomes.

title: Centrosymmetric Molecular Strategy With Quadruple Boron–Nitrogen Heteroarenes Enabling Efficient Ultra‐Narrowband Emission
abstract: ABSTRACT Realizing ultra‐narrowband multiple‐resonance thermally activated delayed fluorescence (MR‐TADF) with long‐wavelength emission remains a formidable challenge due to the increased vibronic coupling and excited‐state relaxation with the extension of π‐conjugated framework. In this contribution, a proof‐of‐concept of centrosymmetric molecular strategy fused with quadruple boron–nitrogen heteroarenes is proposed to develop ultra‐narrowband long‐wavelength MR‐TADF emitters. Thus, two MR‐TADF emitters, called DCz‐MR and DAn‐MR, are prepared and characterized. Compounds DCz‐MR and DAn‐MR exhibit the emission peaks at 562 nm and 518 nm in toluene solution, respectively. Small full‐width at half‐maximum (FWHM) of only 16 nm (0.063 eV) for DCz‐MR and 12 nm (0.055 eV) for DAn‐MR are obtained in toluene, especially 14.2 nm (0.058 eV) for DCz‐MR and 8.2 nm (0.040 eV) for DAn‐MR in hexane. In solution‐processed phosphorescence‐sensitized organic light‐emitting diodes, DAn‐MR delivers a maximum external quantum efficiency of 24.8% with an electroluminescence FWHM of 27 nm. This research work provides a new method for designing ultra‐narrowband long‐wavelength MR‐TADF emitters.

title: Zwitterion‐Regulated Carbazole Phosphonic Acid Self‐Assembled Monolayers via Proton Transfer and Electrostatic Interactions for 21% Organic Solar Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT The efficiency and stability of high‐performance organic solar cells (OSCs) are increasingly determined by the interfacial quality of self‐assembled monolayer (SAM)‐based hole‐selective layers. Carbazole phosphonic‐acid SAMs such as 2PACz are prone to aggregation in alcoholic precursor solutions because of phosphonic‐acid hydrogen bonding and carbazole π–π interactions, leading to incomplete coverage, nonuniform anchoring, and local electrostatic heterogeneity. Here, we incorporate trimethylglycine (TMG) into 2PACz SAMs to induce proton‐transfer‐coupled charge‐state regulation. Through acid–base association, partial proton transfer from 2PACz to TMG alters the protonation state and local electronic environment of 2PACz. At the molecular‐assembly level, this regulation, together with zwitterion‐derived electrostatic interactions, suppresses 2PACz self‐association and improves solution‐state dispersion. At the interfacial‐anchoring level, the increased phosphonate character favors charge‐assisted P–O–M coordination with ITO, enhancing anchoring stability. The resulting 2PACz:TMG layer exhibits improved coverage, surface‐potential homogeneity, and interfacial robustness, reducing recombination and leakage while facilitating charge extraction. D18:L8‐BO binary OSCs achieve a PCE of 20.52%, while ternary devices reach 21.07%. The strategy also shows broad applicability, enables 18.02% efficiency in 1 cm 2 devices, and improves thermal and light stability. These results establish proton‐transfer‐coupled charge‐state regulation as an effective route to simultaneously control molecular assembly, SAM formation uniformity, and interfacial anchoring in phosphonic‐acid SAMs.

title: A New Paradigm for Computational Chemistry
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Computational chemistry has become an indispensable tool for generating data and insights, pervading all branches of experimental chemistry. Its most central concept is the potential energy hypersurface, which is key to all chemistry and materials science, as it assigns an energy to a molecular structure, the necessary ingredient for reaction mechanism elucidation and reaction rate calculation. Density functional theory (DFT) has been the most important method in practice for obtaining such energies, which is reflected in the use of high-performance computing hardware. In the last two decades, a new class of surrogate potential energy functions has evolved with remarkable properties: quantum accuracy combined with force-field speed. Until very recently, their application was hampered by the fact that they needed to be trained on truly large system-specific data sets, generated before a computational chemistry study could be started (in sharp contrast to DFT, which, as a first-principles method, works out of the box but at a far higher price of computational cost). Very recently, this roadblock has been overcome by so-called foundation machine learning interatomic potentials, which are poised to completely change the way we do computational chemistry, likely prompting us to abandon DFT as the prime method of choice for this purpose in less than a decade.

title: Boosting Carrier Mobility and Restoring Ambipolarity in 2D TMD Transistors via Nano-spherical Probe Cleaning
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Two-dimensional (2D) transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs), particularly MoS2 and WSe2, are ideal candidates for constructing next-generation high-performance electronics due to their atomic thickness and excellent electrical tunability. However, interface contaminants and bubbles inevitably introduced during device fabrication remain a critical challenge, acting as scattering centers that severely limit carrier mobility and induce device instability. This study demonstrates an in situ mechanical contact strategy using a nano-spherical probe to precisely remove interface residues in MoS2/hBN and WSe2/hBN van der Waals heterostructures. Experimental results indicate that this method significantly reduces interface roughness from ∼11.5 to ∼1.35 nm. The cleaned MoS2 field-effect transistors (FETs) exhibited a significant increase in effective electron mobility from ∼8.5 to 79.2 cm2/V·s, an improvement of approximately one order of magnitude in the on/off ratio, and a significant suppression of charge-trapping-induced hysteresis. For WSe2 devices, the technique successfully restored intrinsic symmetric ambipolar transport characteristics, enhancing both electron and hole drive currents. Furthermore, a 90-day monitoring period in a non-vacuum environment revealed the different degradation mechanisms of interface adsorbates on n-type and p-type carrier transport. This work not only confirms the universality of nanomechanical cleaning technology in enhancing the intrinsic performance of 2D material heterostructure devices but also deeply elucidates the structure–property relationship regarding long-term stability, providing guidance for the interface engineering of high-performance 2D electronics.

title: High-Mobility a-InZnO Thin-Film Transistors Incorporating an Oxygen-Related Defect Control Layer for Improved Illumination Stability and Environmental Reliability
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The introduction of an appropriate passivation layer is considered a viable strategy for improving the long-term stability and electrical performance of thin-film transistors (TFTs). In this study, an additional layer deposition strategy involving the deposition of a single-layer oxygen-related defect control layer on amorphous indium zinc oxide (a-IZO) thin-film transistors is developed. This approach improves the electrical characteristics and negative-bias illumination stress (NBIS) stability of the channel layer. The oxygen-related defect control layer is a hafnium oxynitride (HfON) layer. It functions as an insulating material with a relatively high dielectric constant, high film density, and low surface energy, serving as a protective barrier against environmental degradation such as exposure to ambient air and moisture. In addition, it contributes to the improvement of NBIS-induced stability by passivating the defect sites in a-IZO during the activation annealing process. Furthermore, the number of carriers in the channel layer increased because of the formation of oxygen vacancies in the a-IZO front channel through the oxygen adsorption of the oxygen-related defect control layer, resulting in the fabrication of thin films with better electrical properties. This resulted in field-effect mobility improving from 37.53 to 66.43 cm2/(V s), the on/off current ratio was enhanced from 1.93 × 109 to 5.77 × 1011, and the threshold voltage shift under NBIS at green light (532 nm) flux density of 1 mW/cm2 for 10,000 s decreased from 15.25 to 2.64 V.

title: Cascade-Catalytic MnO2 Nanoreactor Amplifies Oxidative Stress and Activates cGAS–STING Pathway To Remodel the Immunosuppressive Microenvironment of Triple-Negative Breast Cancer
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC) is characterized by a highly immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment, which severely limits the therapeutic efficacy of current immunotherapies. To address this challenge, we developed a hyaluronic acid-modified tumor-targeted MnO2 nanoreactor (HMGR@HA) for the codelivery of GOx and 20(S)-ginsenoside Rg3 (Rg3), thereby integrating metabolic interference with cascade catalytic therapy and endogenous immune activation. In this system, GOx continuously catalyzed the oxidation of glucose to generate H2O2, which was subsequently converted by MnO2 into highly cytotoxic reactive oxygen species (ROS) while simultaneously producing oxygen. This process established a self-reinforcing catalytic cycle that effectively circumvented the intrinsic limitation of insufficient endogenous H2O2 within the tumor microenvironment. The resulting amplified oxidative stress, in synergy with the chemotherapeutic effect of Rg3, induced profound mitochondrial dysfunction and triggered the cytosolic release of mtDNA. As a potent endogenous danger signal, cytosolic mtDNA robustly activated the cGAS-STING signaling axis, thereby converting localized oxidative damage into strong innate immune activation. In addition, HMGR@HA induced immunogenic cell death (ICD), promoted dendritic cells (DCs) maturation, enhanced infiltration of CD4+ and CD8+ effector T cells, and significantly depleted regulatory T cells (Tregs), collectively leading to extensive remodeling of the tumor immune microenvironment. Ultimately, this self-amplifying catalytic platform effectively drives the transition from localized tumor eradication to systemic antitumor immunity, offering a highly efficient therapeutic strategy for TNBC immunotherapy.

title: Interfacial Chemistry Regulation via Multifunctional Additive for Aqueous Zinc Metal Batteries
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Aqueous zinc metal batteries (AZMBs) are constrained by water-induced side reactions and non-uniform Zn deposition. Herein, we introduce 3,4-dihydroxycyclobut-3-ene-1,2-dione (SA) as an electrolyte additive to regulate molecular interface chemistry. The introduction of SA disrupts the intrinsic hydrogen-bond network in the electrolyte, suppressing the activity of free water. Density functional theory calculations further demonstrate that SA preferentially binds to the Zn (100) and (101) surfaces over the (002) plane, which effectively limits the growth of high-energy facets and promotes oriented nucleation along the (002) texture, yielding a dense and uniform zinc deposit. Benefiting from these synergistic effects, the Zn//Zn symmetric cell achieves a stable cycling lifespan exceeding 2500 h, while the Zn//Cu asymmetric cell maintains a high Coulombic efficiency of 99.4% over 1000 cycles. This work offers an effective pathway for enhancing the performance of AZMBs.

title: Half-Cycle-Selective Thermal Activation Decouples Oxide Quality from Interfacial Oxidation in Atomic Layer Deposition
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract As semiconductor devices approach nanometer-scale dimensions, functional oxide integration increasingly requires the simultaneous improvement of oxide quality and preservation of chemically fragile interfaces. Conventional atomic layer deposition (ALD) imposes a single substrate temperature on all half-reactions, creating an intrinsic trade-off in which thermal conditions that densify and crystallize oxides also accelerate oxidant-driven interfacial oxidation. Temporal thermal-budget engineering is introduced as a route to break this coupling by selectively positioning intense pulsed light (IPL)-induced transient thermal activation within the ALD cycle. Placing IPL before the metal precursor pulse activates precursor-related surface reactions, while allowing the substrate to cool before the subsequent O3 pulse. This half-cycle-resolved thermal control reduces impurities, increases film density, and promotes tetragonal ZrO2 crystallization at 220 °C, while avoiding pronounced interfacial oxidation on oxidation-sensitive electrodes such as TiN, Mo, and W. The resulting ZrO2 films exhibit a dielectric constant of ∼33 with a small interfacial equivalent oxide thickness. This concept is extended to HfO2 ALD on Mo, and its applicability to high-aspect-ratio trenches is verified by crystalline ZrO2 formation with comparable crystallinity along sidewall and bottom regions. These results establish temporal thermal-budget engineering as a broadly applicable strategy for oxide integration on oxidation-sensitive electrodes and complex three-dimensional architectures.

title: Dual-Interface Engineering of Cs2CuBiBr6-Based Memristive Synaptic Devices for Neuromorphic Computing
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Pb-free double perovskite Cs2CuBiBr6 (CCBB)-based resistive random-access memory (ReRAM) synaptic devices are developed using a dual-interface engineering approach to achieve stable resistive switching and neuromorphic functionality. High-quality CCBB thin films are obtained via optimized antisolvent-assisted crystallization, enabling enhanced crystallinity and reduced defect-induced energetic disorder. Modification of the bottom interface with a poly(3,4-ethylenedioxythiophene) polystyrene sulfonate (PEDOT:PSS) interlayer improves CCBB film continuity and provides a more favorable environment for homogeneous charge injection. The introduction of an ultrathin bathocuproine (BCP) interlayer at the top interface regulates the spatial redistribution of Ag-related species. The cooperative regulation of charge injection and Ag-related electro-ionic processes promotes more reproducible formation and rupture of localized conductive pathways, resulting in improved switching stability and device-to-device reproducibility. The CCBB-based ReRAM exhibits reliable bipolar resistive switching over 600 cycles, an on/off current ratio of approximately 103, and stable data retention up to 104 s. Gradual and repeatable conductance modulation under electrical pulse stimulation further demonstrates synaptic potentiation and depression behaviors. MNIST-based neural network simulations reveal excellent neuromorphic performance, with up to 90% recognition accuracy. This work highlights cooperative dual-interface regulation of charge injection and Ag-related electro-ionic processes as an effective design strategy for achieving reliable Pb-free perovskite ReRAM and neuromorphic synaptic operation.

title: Tumor-Microenvironment-Activated DOX@Cu2S@PDA@MnO2 Nanoplatform for MRI/PAI-Assisted Chemophotothermal Therapy of Osteosarcoma
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Osteosarcoma remains difficult to treat because surgery and chemotherapy can provide incomplete tumor control, cause systemic toxicity, and lack reliable local monitoring. In this study, a tumor-microenvironment-activated DOX@Cu2S@PDA@MnO2 nanoplatform was prepared by converting Cu2O nanocubes into hollow Cu2S, coating polydopamine, growing a MnO2 shell, and loading doxorubicin. The Cu2S/PDA structure enabled strong NIR absorption and drug loading, while MnO2 responded to acidic H2O2/GSH-rich conditions to promote O2 generation, ROS-related reactions, and enhanced T1 MRI contrast. The nanoplatform showed concentration-dependent photothermal conversion at 808 and 1024 nm, microenvironment-responsive DOX release, increased intracellular ROS, and stronger killing of 143B osteosarcoma cells under NIR irradiation than carrier or free-drug controls. In tumor-bearing mice, it enhanced MRI/photoacoustic signals, enabled local photothermal heating, markedly inhibited tumor growth, and increased H&E-defined tumor damage and TUNEL-positive apoptosis, especially with 1024 nm irradiation. Hemolysis, organ histology, hematology, and blood biochemistry indicated acceptable short-term safety after repeated intratumoral administration. These results support this Cu2S/PDA/MnO2-based platform for imaging-guided localized osteosarcoma therapy.

title: A Dual pH‑Responsive Hydrogel with Site‑Specific Therapeutic Functions for Differential Pathological Microenvironment Remodeling and Accelerated Repair of Infected Diabetic Wounds
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Diabetic skin wounds have disrupted local acid–base balance, prone to bacterial adhesion and sustained chronic inflammation that hinders tissue repair. Benefiting from the unique properties of oxidized sodium alginate, we prepared a dual pH-responsive Schiff base crosslinked hydrogel loaded with herbal nanoparticles to remodel the defective wound microenvironment and speed up regeneration. Dynamic covalent crosslinking endows the hydrogel with favorable flexibility and shape adaptability to fit irregular wound surfaces. It exhibits obvious dual pH sensitivity: strong antibacterial activity in bacteria-rich acidic niches and slow hydrolysis under diabetic wound alkalinity, achieving stable drug release without burst leakage. The encapsulated nanoparticles exhibit multiple complementary functions. Zn2+ acts as an efficient bactericide to eliminate pathogens. L-Arginine facilitates nitric oxide (NO) generation to promote angiogenesis and M2 macrophage polarization. The glycyrrhetinic acid-2-hydroxyacetophenone conjugate (GA-HAP) suppresses proinflammatory cytokines to relieve local inflammation. In vitro and in vivo experiments verify that this composite hydrogel balances wound pH, eradicates bacterial infection, and mitigates persistent inflammation, remarkably accelerating diabetic wound healing. This pH-sensitive herbal hydrogel holds great potential for microenvironment regulation and clinical therapy of intractable diabetic wounds.

title: A Diabetic Wound Microenvironment-Responsive HAMA-PBA/PVA Hydrogel for Localized Delivery of Netrin-1-Enriched Adipose-Derived Stem Cell-Derived Exosomes Promotes Diabetic Wound Healing through Immunomodulation and Angiogenesis
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Diabetic wounds are characterized by persistent inflammation, endothelial dysfunction, impaired angiogenesis, and poor local retention of therapeutic agents, all of which hinder effective repair. Here, we combined Netrin-1-enriched exosomes (NTN-Exos) from genetically modified adipose-derived stem cells with a photo-crosslinkable phenylboronic acid-modified hyaluronic acid methacryloyl/polyvinyl alcohol (HAMA-PBA/PVA) hydrogel to create a diabetic wound-responsive exosome–hydrogel system. NTN-Exos@Gel enabled prolonged local exosome retention owing to its favorable injectability, biocompatibility, and pH- and reactive oxygen species-responsive degradation and release behavior. In vitro, NTN-Exos reduced high-glucose-induced endothelial apoptosis and restored endothelial migration, proliferation, and tube-forming capacity. Additionally, NTN-Exos reduced inflammatory reactions and promoted macrophage polarization toward a reparative phenotype. NTN-Exos@Gel dramatically accelerated wound closure, improved blood perfusion, boosted neovascularization, improved re-epithelialization and collagen deposition, and decreased local inflammatory cytokine production in a diabetic full-thickness wound model. Mechanistically, transcriptome and protein analysis showed that the pro-angiogenic action of NTN-Exos was associated with altered Hippo signaling, which is typified by higher YAP/TAZ expression, decreased phosphorylation of LATS1 and YAP, and increased expression of CD146. These results suggest that NTN-Exos@Gel is a viable cell-free approach for the healing of diabetic wounds.

title: Thermal Transport in Atomic Layer Deposition-Grown Beryllium Oxide Thin Films and Implications on Device Cooling
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Thin film beryllium oxide (BeO) is an emerging material that can potentially be used as a high thermal conductivity gate dielectric and/or passivation layer for high power electronic devices. This study presents the measurement of the thermal conductivity and thermal boundary conductance associated with plasma-enhanced atomic layer deposition (PEALD)-grown polycrystalline BeO films on Si substrates with thicknesses ranging from 25 to 250 nm. The measured out-of-plane thermal conductivities of the 250, 113, 53, and 26 nm-thick BeO films are 13.45 ± 1.45, 8.7 ± 1.35, 7.2 ± 2.1, and 5 ± 2.2 W m–1 K–1, respectively, representing an order-of-magnitude improvement over conventional dielectric materials such as SiN and SiO2. The measured thermal boundary conductance across the BeO/Si interface is ∼200 MW m–2 K–1 at room temperature, which approaches the intrinsic interface limit and suggests that interfacial heat transport is predominantly governed by elastic phonon transmission. The growth of a ∼200 nm-thick polycrystalline diamond film on an AlGaN/GaN-on-Si epitaxial wafer using a 5 nm-thick BeO diamond-seeding is demonstrated, where the structural integrity of the underlying AlGaN/GaN heterostructure is fully preserved. Thermal simulations of AlGaN/GaN high electron mobility transistors (HEMTs) integrated with a top-side polycrystalline diamond heat spreader predict that replacing the conventional SiO2 passivation and nucleation layers with BeO helps reduce the channel temperature rise by an additional 5.2%.

title: ROS-Responsive Hydrogel for Spatiotemporal Cascade Regulation of Ferroptosis and Fibrosis for Myocardial Protection
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Myocardial infarction (MI)-induced cardiac injury is mainly divided into two phases: the acute necrotic phase and the repair phase. Given the distinct therapeutic requirements of each phase—salvaging dying cardiomyocytes and reducing infarct size in the acute phase, while achieving controlled fibrosis to promote effective ventricular remodeling in the repair phase—we designed an ROS-responsive hydrogel co-delivery system (Met/Anti-34a@Gel) loaded with metformin (Met) and Anti-34a liposomes (Anti-34a Lip) to achieve precise regulation of both the acute and repair phases of MI. In the highly oxidative stress microenvironment following MI, the hydrogel gradually degrades and releases Met and Anti-34a Lip in a stage-specific manner. Met improves mitochondrial function, inhibits oxidative stress and ferroptosis, thereby effectively salvaging cardiomyocytes in the acute phase. Anti-34a Lip modulates the differentiation behavior of cardiac fibroblasts, suppressing excessive fibrosis and promoting favorable ventricular remodeling in the repair phase. Echocardiography revealed that Met/Anti-34a@Gel preserved left ventricular ejection fraction (EF) and fractional shortening (FS) at 72 h post-MI, reduced serum MDA levels in the acute phase, and maintained EF at approximately 60.92 ± 8.37% with a lower collagen I/III ratio at 4 weeks, collectively demonstrating both acute cardioprotection and long-term anti-fibrotic remodeling. In this combined therapeutic strategy, the early mitochondrial protection and anti-ferroptosis effects establish a favorable tissue and functional foundation for subsequent precision anti-fibrotic therapy, while the later anti-fibrotic treatment further consolidates the early protective effects. The two actions synergistically form a positive feedback loop, ultimately achieving sustained long-term cardiac functional improvement.

title: Butterfly wing patterns make motion hard to read
abstract: Movement can expose camouflaged prey, yet whether colour patterns help moving prey to avoid capture is a long-standing puzzle. Butterfly wings might offer an answer.

title: Invisible Patterned Silver-Based Transparent Electrodes via Control of Light Scattering and Absorption
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The demand for transparent flexible electrodes (TFEs) with superior simultaneous optical, electrical, and mechanical performance beyond indium tin oxide (ITO) has driven the development of various nanostructured architectures. Metal-based patterned surfaces have become strong contenders in the TFEs field due to their significantly higher mechanical flexibility; however, their current use is, in part, limited by their scattering-induced visibility to the naked eye. Herein, we report polymeric web-assisted two-dimensional nanostructures, fabricated via electrospinning and integrated with gas-phase deposition methods such as magnetron sputtering, yielding thin film nanopatterning with ultra-high luminous transmittance (Tlum) of 98.1% and sheet resistance (Rs) of 17 Ω □–1. The addition of an antireflective coating enhances the Tlum to 99.7%. The designed trilayer, highly absorbing Fabry–Perot stack (Ag/ITO/NiCr) sputtered on patterned nanolines (NLs) leads to backward scattering suppression, rendering them significantly less visible than the “uncloaked” Ag-only NLs. Our findings are confirmed by finite-difference time-domain (FDTD) simulations. These high-performing, near-invisible electrodes allow for adjustable conductivity through thickness control without compromising transparency, while maintaining mechanical robustness under bending.
