They are also compatible with polymeric substrates, requiring only room-temperature polymer template dissolution, eliminating the need for high-temperature annealing and representing a promising route toward next-generation optoelectronic applications, including displays, photovoltaics, and wearable electronics.

title: Wettability-Gradient Interphase for Reconciling Water Shielding with Zincate Transport in Alkaline Zn–Ni Batteries
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Artificial interfacial layers on Zn anodes are a promising route for stabilizing alkaline Zn–Ni batteries, but their practical effectiveness is often limited by a trade-off between suppressing water-induced parasitic reactions and maintaining rapid Zn-containing species transport. Herein, a hydrophobic–hydrophilic gradient composite layer is developed on a Zn substrate through sequential perfluorooctyltrichlorosilane (PFOTS) modification followed by crosslinked polyvinyl alcohol (PVA) coating. This gradient interphase couples a buried hydrophobic PFOTS layer with an outer hydrophilic PVA layer, thereby balancing water shielding, electrolyte affinity, mechanical compliance, and Zn-containing species transport at the Zn/electrolyte interface. As a result, the symmetric cell based on PFOTS/PVA-modified Zn (ZP) delivers stable cycling for 1200 h at 1 mA cm–2 and 1 mAh cm–2. When coupled with a Ni(OH)2-based cathode, the resulting alkaline Zn–Ni full cell exhibits an output voltage of ≈1.77 V, retains 93.2% of its capacity after resting for 48 h, sustains stable operation for more than 1100 h at 1 C, and maintains durable cycling over 1500 cycles at 2 C. This work demonstrates that wettability-gradient interfacial engineering can reconcile water regulation, Zn-containing species transport, and mechanical compliance for durable alkaline Zn anodes.

title: Interfacial Regulation via Organic-Inorganic Interpenetrating Networks for Enhanced Protection in Waterborne Polyurethane Nanocomposites
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The abundance of hydrophilic groups and the linear polymer chain structure in waterborne polyurethane (WPU) lead to insufficient water resistance and corrosion protection. These inherent characteristics make it challenging for WPU to be applied in the marine protection field, where high comprehensive performance of coatings is demanded. Herein, a WPU nanocomposite was designed incorporating hydroxyl-terminated polydimethylsiloxane and bifunctionalized nano-silica (modified with 3-aminopropyltriethoxysilane and propyltrimethoxysilane) during prepolymerization. This strategy established an organic–inorganic interpenetrating cross-linked network through covalent bonding and intermolecular interactions. The silica nanoparticles act as interfacial bridges between polymer segments, mitigating phase separation and agglomeration caused by polarity mismatch, thereby enhancing coating compactness and improving stress transfer. Performance tests demonstrate that the properties of the coating have been comprehensively enhanced. The coating exhibits an elongation at break of 254.64% while maintaining a tensile strength of 21.17 MPa. Additionally, the water absorption rate of the coating decreases to approximately 5%, the electrochemical protection efficiency reaches 99.9920%, and no obvious corrosion phenomenon is observed after a 7 day salt spray corrosion test. Additionally, the coating shows excellent drag-reduction performance, with a drag-reduction rate of 6.56% under turbulent flow. By integrating interfacial design with nanocomposite architecture, this work develops a robust WPU coating system suitable for marine engineering applications, and employs molecular dynamics simulations to reveal the microscopic mechanism by which amino and n-propyl silane dual modification inhibits the aggregation of silica nanoparticles as well as the interfacial interaction mechanism, thereby highlighting the role of colloidal and nanomaterial strategies in advancing functional protective coatings.

title: Porous, Interface-Rich MnOx/α-Al2O3 Nanocatalyst for Chemical Upcycling of PET Plastic Waste
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Interface engineering is a pivotal strategy for achieving superior thermochemical stability and distinct acid-base and redox active sites in heterogeneous nanocatalysts. We report a morphology-controlled, porous MnOx/α-Al2O3 nanocatalyst with well-defined interfaces for efficient chemical upcycling of PET waste bottles into a high-value monomer, bis-(hydroxy neopentyl) terephthalate (BHNT), using neopentyl glycol. Electron microscopy analysis confirmed the high dispersion of MnOx nanoparticles (90 ± 10 nm) on porous α-Al2O3 nanosheets (length: 2800–5050 nm and width: 780–970 nm). This unique heterostructure combination provided intimate interfaces between MnOx and α-Al2O3, facilitating stronger acid sites (especially Lewis acidity) and Mn2+/Mn4+ active sites. The interface-rich MnOx/α-Al2O3 nanocatalyst demonstrated excellent activity in PET upcycling, yielding 90% isolated BHNT monomer. The MnOx/α-Al2O3 catalyst exhibited good reusability up to 4 cycles, with only an 8% decrease in BHNT yield. The crystal structure, morphology, porosity, and interfaces remain unchanged during the reaction, as confirmed by the spent catalyst’s analysis. The potential of the BHNT monomer was demonstrated by polyurethane synthesis, offering a truly circular plastic economy. The versatile properties and remarkable efficiency of the MnOx/α-Al2O3 nanocatalyst, along with sustainable green chemistry metrics, underscore the vital role of interface engineering in heterogeneous catalysts for the plastic recycling industry.

title: Molecule-Driven Unusual Incommensurate Modulation in a 2D Hybrid Perovskite Ferroelectric
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Incommensurate modulation has been extensively investigated in inorganic oxides, representing an emerging frontier in aperiodic materials that enables the discovery of novel quantum phenomena and the manipulation of physical properties, whereas it remains largely unexplored in hybrid perovskites (HPs). Here, we present the driving of successive dynamic rotation of the interlayer dipoles in a two-dimensional HP ferroelectric (DFBZ)2(FA)Pb2I7 (DFBZ is 2,5-difluorobenzylammonium, FA is formamidinium), which enables an unusual incommensurate modulated structure between the paraelectric and ferroelectric phases. Specifically, (DFBZ)2(FA)Pb2I7 exhibits an incommensurate modulated state over a broad temperature range of 313–370 K, and transforms to commensurate modulation at 400–474 K. The incommensurate superstructure at 330 K is ∼6 times larger than its periodic prototype, and its structure can be solved using a (3 + 1)D superspace group with a modulation wavevector of q = (1, 0, 0.1578). The inorganic layers feature a pronounced undulation, while the interlayer organic cations are trapped in distinct rotational states. To the best of our knowledge, (DFBZ)2(FA)Pb2I7 is the first HP ferroelectric that exhibits such a long-range ordered incommensurate modulation. Moreover, its large spontaneous polarization (9.4 μC cm–2) and the near-room temperature ferroelectric-to-incommensurate phase transition result in a giant pyroelectric coefficient of 7.41 μC cm–2 K–1. This unusual incommensurate modulation in HP ferroelectrics offers new insights into the understanding of aperiodic materials and ferroelectric mechanisms.

title: In Situ Tracking of Se Vacancy-Promoted Surface Reconstruction of NiCoSe2 into NiCoOOH during Alkaline Oxygen Evolution
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Understanding the dynamic surface reconstruction of precatalyst materials during the oxygen evolution reaction (OER) is a forefront area of research for designing and studying effective electrocatalysts. Here, we report the deliberate engineering of Se vacancies in NiCoSe2 via a facile NaBH4 reduction strategy and systematically investigate how anion vacancies govern surface reconstruction behavior under alkaline OER conditions. The presence of Se vacancies is confirmed via EPR spectroscopy and ICP-MS analysis. Cyclic voltammetry and in situ electrochemical impedance spectroscopy during the electrochemical activation process reveal that the vacancy-enriched NiCoSe2–x undergoes faster and more extensive structural reconstruction than pristine NiCoSe2. Quasi in situ ATR-FTIR and Raman spectroscopy track the dynamic evolution of NiCoOOH during anodic polarization, providing direct spectroscopic evidence for the Se vacancy-promoted NiCoOOH active phase generation with abundant Ni–O–Co synergy. Evaluation of electrochemical surface area and turnover frequency establishes that the generation of abundant Ni–O–Co synergy in NiCoSe2–x simultaneously increases the density of accessible active sites and enhances the intrinsic activity per site. Consequently, the NiCoSe2–x precatalyst delivers significantly improved OER performance relative to bare NiCoSe2, along with high Faradaic selectivity and long-term stability. Post-stability characterizations confirm bulk structural and morphological reconstruction driven by Se vacancies and thus highlight the complete utilization of the available catalytic sites. This work provides a fundamental mechanistic framework linking anion vacancy engineering, surface reconstruction kinetics/mechanism tracking, and intrinsic OER activity enhancement in bimetallic chalcogenide precatalysts, offering rationalized design principles for next-generation earth-abundant OER catalysts.

title: Three-Dimensional Crosslinked CNT/SiO x -F Network Encapsulated by Pitch-Derived Carbon as a High-Stable Anode for Lithium-Ion Batteries
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Intrinsic low conductivity and huge volume expansion severely limit the cycling stability of SiOx anodes. Herein, a 3D crosslinked CNT/SiOx-F@C composite is synthesized via bifunctional fluorosilane crosslinkers and conformal pitch carbon coating. Fluorosilane acts as both a silicon source and a crosslinker to build interconnected, conductive CNT frameworks, while the outer pitch carbon optimizes the pore structure and induces flexible, LixPOyF6-rich SEI layers. Kinetic tests reveal dominant capacitive charge storage and a Li+ diffusion coefficient one-order-of-magnitude higher than that of control electrodes. The half-cell delivers a stable reversible capacity of 672.6 mA h g–1 over 200 cycles at 0.2 A g–1 and retains 86.5% capacity after 600 cycles at 1 A g–1. Pre-lithiation elevates the initial Coulombic efficiency from 47.4 to 84.2%, while the electrode achieves an areal capacity approaching 4 mA h cm–2, far exceeding that of commercial graphite. This dual-carbon synergistic strategy provides a facile route to optimizing silicon oxide anodes.

title: Intranasal Delivery of an Antioxidant Nanoassembly for Cerebral Ischemia-Reperfusion Injury via Drd2/β-arrestin2/ERK Signaling
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Cerebral ischemia–reperfusion injury (CIRI) is caused by reduced cerebral blood flow, leading to excessive oxidative stress and neurological deficits. Curcumin (Cur) is a promising therapeutic agent, but its antioxidant activity is limited by low bioavailability and poor brain penetration. Herein, an intranasal delivery strategy using a tetrahedral framework nucleic acid (tFNAs)–Cur nanoassembly (tFNAs–Cur) was employed for CIRI treatment. tFNAs–Cur was synthesized through self-assembly, achieving a high Cur loading efficiency of 87% and exhibiting potent scavenging activity against reactive oxygen species (ROS) including O2·–, ·OH, and H2O2. In vitro studies showed that tFNAs–Cur inhibited oxygen glucose deprivation/reoxygenation-induced ROS elevation of cytoplasm and mitochondria, and enhanced proliferation and migration of SH-SY5Y cells. In vivo studies demonstrated that intranasal administration of tFNAs–Cur reduced cerebral infarct volume, enhanced neuronal survival, and improved neurological and behavioral outcomes in middle cerebral artery occlusion rats. Further mechanistic investigation using RNA sequencing revealed that tFNAs–Cur exerted its effects by activating the Drd2/β-arrestin2/ERK signaling, thereby improving mitochondrial function and upregulating BDNF levels. Furthermore, hemolysis assays, serum biochemical measurements, and histopathological analyses demonstrated that tFNAs–Cur possessed a favorable biosafety profile both ex vivo and in vivo. This study provides an intranasal antioxidant nanoassembly strategy for CIRI and holds potential for clinical translation.

title: Recent Advances in Graphene-Based Aerogels for Electromagnetic Wave Absorption: A Comprehensive Review
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract With the rapid development of high-frequency communications, smart electronic devices and aerospace, the problem of electromagnetic interference has become increasingly severe, creating an urgent need for electromagnetic waves (EMWs) absorbing materials that combine high absorption efficiency, broadband response, light weight, and environmental stability. Graphene-based aerogels (GAs) show great promise for EMWs absorption due to their three-dimensional (3D) porous structure, tunable conductivity and surface chemistry, and lightweight high-strength properties. However, existing reviews on EMWs absorbing materials based on GAs have not systematically summarized the synergistic mechanisms between GAs and other materials, nor have they provided an in-depth discussion of optimization strategies for the coordinated regulation of composition and structure. This review comprehensively summarizes the latest research advances in GAs-based EMWs absorbing, explores the fundamental principles of EMWs absorption, and highlights the properties, structural characteristics, and preparation methods of graphene and GAs. In addition, the study examined the effects of defect engineering, multicomponent composites, and structural design (core–shell and heterostructures) on the regulation of EMWs absorption properties. These strategies synergistically yield broad bandwidth and strong attenuation. The review also analyzes the application of GAs in EMWs absorption under special conditions, and discusses the potential use of artificial intelligence (AI) and machine learning in EMWs absorbing materials. Finally, this review discusses the current challenges and future directions for GA-based EMWs absorbing materials, with the aim of establishing relationships between synthesis, structure, and function, filling gaps in existing reviews, and providing guidance for the future development of EMWs absorbing materials.

title: Balancing the Performance Trade-off of Polymer Blends with Heterogeneously Dispersed Nanodomains via Reactive Processing
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Polymer blends are ubiquitous though there are persistent material-property trade-offs, due to the limitation of structural design. Here we report a reactive processing strategy that creates heterogeneously dispersed nano-domains (hDNs) of rubbery ethylene-acrylic ester-glycidyl methacrylate terpolymer (EGMA) in polyoxymethylene (POM) matrix. Pre-reactive blending of EGMA with poly (L-lactide) (PLLA) and subsequent melt processing with POM result in formation of the unique morphology, where PLLA serving as the leveraging forces for opposing uniform distribution via chemical bonds and macro-phase separation by physical associations. The resulting materials exhibited optimized mechanical performance impossible to be acquired with conventional counterparts. This work identifies herein innovates how reactive processing can regulate phase morphology while balancing the trade-off among toughness, ductility, strength and stiffness in multicomponent polymer blends, representing a paradigm shift in narrowing gap between structure and tailor-made property towards pilot plant scale.

title: Lightweight and Robust Bamboo Fiber Composite for Efficient Infrared Stealth
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract With the continuous advancement in modern infrared detection technologies, efficient infrared stealth materials with features of lightweight and high mechanical strength are urgently desired in many fields. In this study, natural bamboo fibers were employed as a renewable substrate and were processed into lightweight and robust infrared stealth bamboo fibrous (HsIs-Bamboo) via oxidative defibration, ionic cross-linking, vacuum-assisted loading, and hot pressing. The fabricated bamboo fibrous composite enables uniform dispersion of functional particles, resulting in low infrared emissivity (65–73% in 8–14 μm), lightweight (0.80 g cm–3), and high mechanical strength (specific tensile strength of 385.9 MPa cm3 g–1). The composite also exhibits low-cost, efficient flame retardancy, and superior infrared shielding performance with a 10.6 °C decrease in the infrared thermal imaging test. This novel infrared stealth material from natural bamboo offers a promising solution for the stealth protection of critical facilities and holds substantial application potential as a highly robust infrared stealth material in weight-sensitive circumstances.

title: Comprehensive spectroscopic analysis of energy inversion of the lowest singlet and triplet excited states in the heptazine HzTFEX2
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Detailed photophysical measurements of the non-symmetric heptazine, HzTFEX2, previously reported as having inverted S1-T1 levels, show complex behaviour, highly dependent on environment, concentration and aggregation. Here we show that, single crystals of HzTFEX2 show anti-Kasha S0←S2 and excimer emission. Solution state absorption shows a hypsochromic shift of the π-π* S0→S1, linearly dependent on solvent polarizability. In most environments, emission is dominated by excimer species, only in toluene and frozen 2-MeTHF do monomeric properties dominate. In frozen solutions, aggregation phenomena are solvent dependent. Given such complexity, time-dependent emission spectra are crowded, making it difficult to resolve monomeric phosphorescence. However, by exciting S0→S2 at 77 K, we observe a consistent phosphorescence signal at 425 nm, 110 ± 20 meV above the S0←S1 emission, whereas exciting S0→S1 does not give phosphorescence or delayed fluorescence (DF). We conclude that coupling between S2 and S1 is very weak, S2-TN intersystem crossing is effective, whereas S1↔T1 intersystem crossing is thermally activated, fulfilling the conditions required for the observation of inverted phosphorescence. At room temperature, no long-lived DF is observed because exothermic T1→S1 ISC becomes allowed, such that in an OLED, high efficiency can be achieved.

title: Strong field spectroscopy of many-body interactions in solids
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: High-order harmonic generation (HHG) in solids offers a promising route to compact ultrafast sources of quantum light, but its efficiency and coherence are limited by ultrafast dephasing of laser-driven electron–hole polarization. Although widely described by a phenomenological coherence time, the microscopic origin of this dephasing has remained unresolved. Here, we combine wavelength-dependent HHG measurements in monolayer and bulk semiconductors with ab initio many-body calculations of electron–phonon scattering and strong-field simulations. We show that the measured wavelength scaling of the HHG yield is quantitatively reproduced only when semiconductor Bloch equations incorporate momentum-dependent dephasing derived from first principles scattering rates. The calculations reveal that strong-field-driven carriers rapidly enter regions of the Brillouin zone with enhanced electron–phonon scattering, giving rise to effective few-femtosecond dephasing. Our results establish a microscopic foundation for dephasing in solid-state HHG and provide a framework for engineering coherence in strongly driven solids for quantum photonic applications.

title: Terahertz emission by X-ray difference-frequency generation
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Nonlinear interactions between X-rays and matter represent a new frontier in ultrafast science. However, X-ray difference-frequency generation (DFG)—a fundamental second-order nonlinear optical process—has not been experimentally observed until now. Here, we report the first observation of terahertz emission induced by hard X-ray free-electron laser (XFEL) pulses in solids, providing evidence for X-ray DFG. Using 10-fs, 10-keV XFEL pulses incident on ZnTe, we detected terahertz emission arising from wave mixing between different spectral components within the XFEL bandwidth. The emitted terahertz waves originate from second-order nonlinear polarization evolving on a femtosecond timescale. The polarization and angular dependences of the terahertz emission confirm that X-ray DFG is mediated not only by DFG without spatial inversion symmetry but also by DFG with spatial inversion symmetry. Quantitative analysis yields a DFG susceptibility ratio of the former to the latter of 58±4%, and the generation efficiency for 10 keV excitation is approximately 1% of that for near-infrared 1.55 eV excitation in the 100-μm-thick ZnTe crystal, while the intrinsic response normalized by interaction length is comparable. These results establish XFEL-induced terahertz emission as a general platform for probing second-order X-ray nonlinearities and ultrafast polarization dynamics in solids.

title: Epithelial NF-κB shapes protective Treg cell responses to restrain intestinal inflammation
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Inflammation resolution depends on coordinated communication between tissue compartments, yet how the intestinal epithelium shapes its immune microenvironment remains poorly understood. Here, using colonic biopsies from patients with ulcerative colitis (UC) and mouse models enabling tissue-wide visualization of NF-κB activity, we combine single-cell RNA sequencing and secretome analysis to define epithelial communication during colitis. We show that, paradoxically, the NF-κB-driven pro-inflammatory secretome of intestinal epithelial cells (IECs) is essential for recovery and prevents unrestrained inflammation. Mechanistically, epithelial NF-κB promotes CCL22-dependent regulatory T cell (Treg cell) recruitment and promotes a tolerogenic, pro-repair cell state, accompanied by induction of the lipid-metabolism-associated GDPD3 and CCR4. In UC, epithelial NF-κB is not uniformly activated but instead induces a selective pro-inflammatory transcriptional program while repressing targets regulating T cell recruitment. Thus, we identify dynamic epithelial–immune communication and demonstrate a protective IEC NF-κB–Treg cell axis important for resolution of intestinal inflammation.

title: Peripheral glia drive the initiation of cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Although tumor innervation is known to promote cancer progression, underlying mechanisms remain poorly understood and have mostly been linked to axonal signaling. Here, we identify peripheral glia as critical drivers of cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (cSCC), the second most common skin cancer in humans. Tumor-associated glial cells (TAGs) resemble embryonic Schwann cell lineage stages, are abundant in the stroma of premalignant lesions and established murine and human cSCC, and are essential for tumor formation. TAG activation in premalignant lesions is triggered by UV-induced anti-inflammatory macrophages, which in turn are polarized by TAGs into pro-tumorigenic FcεRIα⁺ macrophages, key components of the cSCC microenvironment. Consequently, TAG depletion reduces FcεRIα⁺ macrophages, cancer-associated fibroblasts, and epithelial-mesenchymal transition in keratinocytes, thereby impairing cSCC initiation by disrupting intercellular communication required for tumor development. As most solid tumors are innervated and harbor peripheral glia, our findings reveal TAGs as regulators of tumor initiation with potential relevance beyond skin cancer.

title: A prefrontal–bed nucleus pathway controls aversive memory specificity independently of glucocorticoids
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Adaptive memory requires balancing generalization to avoid similar threats with discrimination to recognize safety. The prevailing view is that stress-induced increases in glucocorticoids underlie the enhancement of memory consolidation, strengthening memories and promoting their generalization—referred to here as the standard model. However, circuits that drive memory consolidation often also regulate glucocorticoid release, confounding whether their effects on memory are circuit-driven or hormonally mediated. Here we identify a prefrontal pathway that controls memory specificity independently of glucocorticoids. Using optogenetic manipulations in male rats, we found that post-training inhibition of the rostral prelimbic cortex (rPL) to anteroventral bed nuclei of the stria terminalis (avBST) pathway promoted contextual generalization in an inhibitory avoidance discrimination task without affecting memory strength. Although this manipulation further elevated corticosterone, it produced generalization even in adrenalectomized rats, demonstrating glucocorticoid independence. Conversely, post-training pathway excitation enhanced contextual discrimination. Recordings of calcium signals revealed context-specific engagement of both avBST and avBST-projecting rPL neurons during memory retrieval, with greater responses in the neutral than the aversive context. These findings reveal glucocorticoid-independent circuit control of memory specificity, setting boundary conditions on the standard model and demonstrating mechanistic heterogeneity that may inform stress-related disorders where memory generalization is a core feature.

title: Type I IFN promotes ILC2-to-ILC1 plasticity in pre-clinical radiation-induced lung injury
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Radiation-induced lung injury (RILI) is a common dose-limiting toxicity after radiotherapy for lung cancer, but the immunological mechanisms contributing to RILI pathogenesis remain poorly understood. Here we analyze a RILI mouse model using high-dose, restricted-field irradiation to the left lung. Flow cytometry and cytokine profiling analysis of innate lymphoid cells (ILC) reveals a radiation-induced shift from lung-resident type 2 ILCs (ILC2) toward pro-inflammatory type 1 ILCs (ILC1). Single-cell RNA-sequencing analysis of mouse lung ILC populations after radiation suggests that type I interferon (IFN) promotes radiation-induced ILC2-to-ILC1 plasticity. In vitro, IFN-β stimulation of mouse ILC2s leads to increased expression of the ILC1 markers T-bet and IFN-γ, while IFN-β stimulation of human peripheral blood mononuclear cells increases the ILC1-to-ILC2 ratio. In vivo, inhibition of type I IFN signaling attenuates lung damage after irradiation in our RILI model. Thus, our findings indicate that radiation-induced type I IFN induces ILC2-to-ILC1 plasticity to contribute to RILI pathogenesis, and suggest that targeting type I IFN signaling may be a therapeutic strategy to mitigate radiation-induced lung injury.

title: High-risk antimicrobial resistance genomic traits in multidrug-resistant Salmonella across China’s food chain: projections to 2050
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Antimicrobial resistance (AMR) is rising globally, yet factors shaping its genomic evolution remain poorly understood. We investigated how socioeconomic, climate, and health factors are associated with AMR spread in multi-drug resistant (MDR) Salmonella enterica across China’s food chain, mapped hotspots and forecasted genomic trait prevalence to 2050. We analysed 2,536 MDR genomes from 15 provinces over 16 years, covering patients, food and non-food workers, meat, livestock, and environmental sources. A machine learning framework integrated genomic surveillance with risk assessment to identify high-risk AMR traits (clinically relevant, MDR, mobile). Regression models linked trait prevalence to socioeconomic, climate, health, and antimicrobial consumption data, informing projections to 2050. Eighty-four high-risk traits, including carbapenem, colistin, and β-lactam resistance, are projected to rise, with antibiotic use, population growth, healthcare spending, and urbanisation. Projections were trait-specific: blaCTX-M-64 and blaTEM-1 may increase up to 20%, while blaCTX-M-65 and blaCTX-M-14 remain below 5%. A mechanistic shift in fluoroquinolone resistance is projected: mutation-based resistance (gyrA 87) declines while plasmid-mediated genes (qnrB17, qnrS1) rise. Food workers emerged as a potential reservoir, showing higher trait prevalence than food sources, uniquely carrying last-resort antibiotic-resistance genes (blaTEM-30, blaNDM-5, blaCTX-M-64). Integrating genomic with socioeconomic surveillance could shift AMR interventions from reactive to preventive.

title: G-quadruplex structures affect the immune response to bacterial infection in mouse macrophages
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Macrophages orchestrate immunity via transcriptional reprogramming, largely controlled by the master regulator NF-κB. However, mechanisms of promoter selection remain enigmatic. Here, we reveal that DNA secondary structures called G-quadruplexes (G4s) modulate the macrophage transcriptome during inflammation. By investigating the G4 ligand pyridostatin (PDS) in lipopolysaccharide-stimulated macrophages, we establish that G4 stabilization significantly decreases the inflammatory response without affecting mitochondrial metabolism or pathogen clearance. Instead, NF-κB-dependent transcription of activation markers and proinflammatory cytokines is selectively repressed. Using chromatin accessibility profiling, NF-κB ChIP, and in silico predictions, we demonstrate that G4 stabilization sterically hinders NF-κB promoter occupancy. Furthermore, PDS stabilizes transient, transcription-induced G4s, prematurely shutting down transcription and reverting local chromatin to a dormant state. Thus, G4 formation represents a potential strategy to modulate dysregulated macrophage activation.

title: The Emirati pangenome featuring a diploid chromosome-level reference
source: Scientific community and society : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Reference genomes are essential for identifying and representing human genomic variation, yet single-genome sequences fail to capture population-specific diversity. We present the Emirati pangenome comprising a trio-based, diploid chromosome-level assembly from deep, multi-platform sequencing data and 57 additional high-quality HiFi sequencing-based chromosome-scale assemblies, 27 of which are trio-based. Haplotypes demonstrate high contiguity (median N50 of 151.9 Mb) and good base accuracy (median QV score of 59.31). Of all assembled chromosomes, 31.8% are telomere-to-telomere (T2T) scaffolds (chromosome-spanning sequences flanked by telomeric repeats at both ends), and 64.3% achieved chromosome-level continuity (single scaffolds spanning an entire chromosome but retaining one or more sequence gaps or lacking a telomeric signature at one or both ends). These assemblies form the foundation of the population-specific pangenome graph of the Emirati Reference Genome Project (ERGP), which captures genomic variation comparable to the globally diverse HPRC reference graph, while covering regionally enriched variation. Applying the ERGP pangenome to short‑read genotyping of an independent Emirati cohort revealed structural variant sites in linkage disequilibrium with phenotype‑associated GWAS variants, demonstrating the value of population-graph-based variant inference. The ERGP reference complements human pangenomes and provides a critical foundation for population-specific genomics and precision medicine in the United Arab Emirates.

title: Identification and genetic characterization of megabase-scale plasmids of Enterobacteriaceae
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Humans and animals are ubiquitously colonized by Enterobacteriaceae, including both commensals and clinically significant pathogens. Here, we report 21 complete Enterobacteriaceae megaplasmid genomes of up to 1.58 Mbp in length spanning two major clades that are highly divergent from previously described plasmids. Of these, three were reconstructed from isolates of Escherichia coli and Shigella flexneri; others were potentially hosted by species of Citrobacter and Enterobacter. Related megabase-scale plasmids were detected in at least 400 infant and adult gut, and other microbiomes. Diverse Enterobacteriaceae hosts, conjugation machinery, and DNA modification patterns suggest that these elements are self-transmissible, with a broad host range. The plasmids encode multi-drug efflux systems and potential secreted effectors. Up to 208 tRNAs are encoded and include sequence variants that may counter tRNA-centric defense mechanisms. Overall, the vast plasmid coding capacity may broaden host range, increase competitiveness, control invasion by other elements, and counter programmed cell death.

title: Targeting high-value uses to unlock the mitigation potential of clean hydrogen
abstract: Clean hydrogen is a versatile decarbonization option, but given its energy-intensive production, high costs and limited near-term supply, uses with the greatest environmental and economic benefits must be prioritized. Analysis of ten end-use sectors identifies high-value applications and suggests that uniform supply-side subsidies risk misallocating clean hydrogen and public funds, highlighting the need for sector-specific demand-side policies.

title: Cavity-Selective Host–Guest Assembly for Modular Buried-Interface Engineering in Perovskite Solar Cells
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Buried-interface engineering is critical for inverted perovskite solar cells, yet integrating anchoring, charge transport, electrostatic regulation, and defect passivation within single molecular systems often creates intrinsic trade-offs. Here, we use cavity-selective host–guest recognition to construct a modular, recognition-directed interface. The cavity of dipolar 4-tert-butylsulfonylcalix[4]arene (tBSCA) selectively accommodates the terminal phenyl group of substrate-anchored Ph-4PACz. Comparisons with a structurally related calixarene analogue and competing inclusion orientations identify a thermodynamically preferred Ph-4PACz-tBSCA configuration, distinguishing cavity-selective association from nonspecific interactions. This preferred configuration underpins a preferentially organized dipolar interface that retains Ph-4PACz-mediated anchoring and charge transport while enabling tBSCA to regulate interfacial electrostatics, reduce interfacial defect sites, and suppress defect-assisted halide migration and interfacial accumulation. The resulting devices achieve a PCE of 27.36% (certified at 26.74%), and a 110 cm2 module delivers a certified efficiency of 22.61%. These results demonstrate configuration-selective molecular recognition as a strategy for the modular organization of complementary functions at buried perovskite interfaces.

title: Charge-Density-Dependent Ionomer Effects in Pure-Water CO2 Electrolysis
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Pure-water membrane electrode assemblies (MEAs) represent a promising strategy to eliminate (bi)carbonate salt precipitation for electrochemical CO2 reduction (CO2R). However, the absence of alkali metal cations fundamentally restricts CO2 activation and intermediate stabilization, thereby reducing catalytic performance. Here, we overcome this limitation by identifying the ionomer charge density as a key molecular-level parameter associated with pure-water CO2R. By comparing anion-exchange ionomers with varying charge characteristics, we reveal that high-charge-density ionomer (HCDI) introduces a favorable catalyst–membrane interfacial environment, enabling superior macroscopic CO2R performance. HCDI-enabled MEAs achieve >99% CO Faradaic efficiency at 100 mA cm–2 and sustain ∼92% at 1000 mA cm–2. In situ diagnosis and electrochemical characterization reveal that the HCDI-functionalized interface produces a substantial *CO signal, while concurrently suppressing hydrogen evolution. By decoupling cation effects from liquid electrolytes, these findings support interfacial ionomer charge density as a useful comparative parameter for pure-water CO2 MEA electrolyzers.

title: Macroporous Interlayers Stabilize Long-Lived Hole Polarons in Organic Semiconductor Photoanodes
source: ACS Energy Letters: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Integrating alternative oxidation reactions (AORs) into photoelectrochemical (PEC) systems is promising for unassisted hydrogen production and value-added chemical synthesis, yet organic semiconductor (OS) photoanodes suffer from poor charge extraction and short carrier lifetimes. Here, we address this bottleneck by stabilizing long-lived hole polarons through macroporous tin oxide (mcSnO2) interlayers. Transient absorption spectroscopy reveals that accelerated electron extraction through mcSnO2 stabilizes hole polaron states, substantially prolonging carrier lifetimes. Consequently, the optimized organic photoanodes outperform bare counterparts by more than 5.5-fold, retaining 74% of their initial photocurrent over 15 h for iodide oxidation and 61% over 35 h for ascorbic acid oxidation. Furthermore, integrating this robust organic photoanode with an OS-based photocathode enables the first bias-free organic PEC tandem cell coupling hydrogen evolution with AORs, delivering a remarkable solar-to-hydrogen conversion efficiency of 1.4%. These findings establish interfacial carrier lifetime engineering as an effective strategy for realizing high-performance and durable organic PEC systems.

title: Directed assembly of cathode interlayers enables efficient binary organic solar cells
abstract:
Abstract
                  Cathode interlayers create interfacial dipoles in organic solar cells to maximize device efficiency. However, the dipoles are highly dependent on the molecular orientation of the interlayers, which remain challenging to be controlled. Here, based on the amphiphilic nature of the interlayers, we show a stepwise film deposition approach using a polar solvent for active layer pretreatment and a bipolar solvent for subsequent interlayer self assembly. Sum-frequency generation vibrational spectroscopy reveals a preferred perpendicular orientation of the interlayer molecules, thereby enhancing the surface potential and reducing the charge transport resistance. As a result, we achieve a certified efficiency of 20.65% and fill factor of 82.7% in binary organic solar cells. This method is universally applicable to different cathode interlayers and active layers. Our work highlights the importance of controlling interlayer molecular orientation for unlocking significant performance gains, paving the way for further advancements in device optimization.

title: Stacking-specific two-dimensional In2Se3 for ferroelectric homojunctions
abstract: Stacking-controllable 2D In2Se3 grown by chemical vapour deposition reveals a strong dependence of ferroelectricity on stacking order. A 2H/3R homojunction memristor achieves an on/off ratio one order of magnitude higher than that of pure-phase devices, offering opportunities for advanced ferroelectric memory applications.

title: Supramolecular chemical ligation of helical polymers
abstract: Chemical ligation of synthetic polymers is achieved via supramolecular polymerization followed by dynamic covalent polycondensation in a process that does not require thermal activation.

title: Tuning Interfacial Electron Transfer for Boosting Electrochemiluminescence: Methods, Mechanisms, and Bioanalytical Applications
abstract: Abstract The interfacial electron-transfer process acts as a pivotal kinetic determinant of electrochemiluminescence (ECL) efficiency, governing the generation of excited-state emitters and thus dictating the intensity and stability of ECL signals. Currently, harnessing diverse nanomaterials has driven significant advances in the development of novel ECL luminophores and the activation of coreactants. However, most of these luminophores exhibit low ECL efficiency in aqueous media, and the intrinsic reaction and activation mechanisms remain ambiguous because of their complex structures and compositions. Notably, tuning electron-transfer pathways at the molecular/atomic level can not only enable efficient signal amplification but also facilitate the tracking of reaction pathways, thereby providing deeper insights into the fundamental mechanisms underlying ECL processes. This Review comprehensively summarizes advances during the past five years in tuning interfacial electron transfer to enhance ECL. Furthermore, we highlight progress in electron-transfer-mediated signal amplification strategies for highly sensitive ECL biosensing and bioimaging applications. Finally, we propose and discuss the challenges and perspectives associated with improving the ECL efficiency through the modulation of electron transfer processes. Precise regulation of interfacial electron transfer holds substantial promise for advancing ECL theories, clarifying reaction mechanisms, and expanding the scope of ECL-based bioanalytical applications.

title: Author Correction: Rice–fish co-culturing reduces schistosomiasis risk and increases yields and incomes
Three-photon population imaging of subcortical brain regions
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Monitoring large-scale neuronal activity in deep brain circuits is crucial for understanding the principles of brain function. However, existing large-scale cellular-resolution imaging techniques are limited in imaging depth and cannot monitor activity in areas deeper than the cortex in the intact brain. To address this challenge, we developed a Large Imaging Field of view Three-photon (LIFT) microscope with a FOV of > 3 mm2. LIFT combines high-numerical-aperture optimized sampling, using a custom scanning module, with deep learning-based denoising, to enable population imaging in subcortical brain regions of mice and deep cortical regions of rats. We demonstrate calcium imaging in the intact mouse brain from more than 1500 cells across CA1, the surrounding white matter, and adjacent deep layers of the cortex, and show population imaging with high SNR at a depth of 1.2 mm in the rat cortex. The LIFT microscope offers versatility in imaging scale and rate and was built entirely from off-the-shelf components.

title: Oncogenic signalling and host immunocompetency govern senescent cell clearance and systemic inflammation in a mouse model of oncogene-induced senescence
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Senescence is a stress-induced program defined by permanent cell-cycle arrest and a pro-inflammatory senescence-associated secretory phenotype (SASP). Defective clearance of senescent cells promotes inflammation, tissue dysfunction, and ageing, yet determinants of their elimination remain poorly understood. Here, we model oncogene-induced senescence in the hematopoietic system by transplanting BrafV600E- or BrafΔN-expressing hematopoietic stem and progenitor cells into recipients with distinct immune backgrounds. BrafV600E induces a stronger senescence program and more aggressive disease than BrafΔN. Survival depends on oncogene-expressing cell burden and host immunity: immunocompetent, lower-burden mice clear oncogene-expressing cells and survive long-term, whereas higher-burden mice show checkpoint upregulation, T-cell exhaustion, and early death. NSG, Rag1KO, and lymphocyte-depleted hosts fail to clear these cells, developing sustained inflammation and bone marrow failure. Rapamycin administration attenuates senescence-associated features and improves survival. These findings identify oncogenic intensity and adaptive immune competence as coupled determinants of senescent-cell fate, with implications for chronic inflammation and senescence-targeted therapies.

title: Exploring healthy aging through preclinical Alzheimer disease in the Knight Alzheimer Research Imaging dataset
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Alzheimer disease (AD) remains a significant global public health challenge, requiring robust multimodal datasets to elucidate its prolonged preclinical phase, improve early detection, advance understanding of disease trajectories, and guide intervention strategies. Here we present the Knight Alzheimer Research Imaging (KARI) dataset, established by the Washington University Knight ADRC to address this critical need. We detail comprehensive multimodal neuroimaging from 1,645 participants (aged 42-97) across 6,217 acquisitions. Spanning the AD spectrum from healthy aging to symptomatic disease, the cohort undergoes extensive longitudinal imaging using structural and functional magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) alongside positron emission tomography (PET) tracers for amyloid and tau pathology. This is complemented by rich clinical, cognitive, genetic, and biomarker data. In addition to raw imaging, the dataset provides quality-controlled processed outputs, including anatomical segmentations and biomarker quantification. By making this data accessible to researchers, the Knight ADRC aims to accelerate discoveries in pathophysiology, biomarker identification, and therapeutic development.

title: Direct observation of the Lindhard continuum using resonant inelastic X-ray scattering
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Understanding the excitations of quantum materials is essential for unraveling how their microscopic constituents interact. Among these, particle-hole excitations form a particularly important class, as they govern fundamental processes such as screening, dissipation, and transport. In metals, the continuum of electron-hole excitations is described by the Lindhard function. Although central to the theory of Fermi liquids, the corresponding Lindhard continuum has remained experimentally elusive. Here we report its direct observation in the weakly correlated metal MgB2 using ultra-soft resonant inelastic X-ray scattering. We resolve a linearly dispersing excitation with velocity comparable to the Fermi velocity and find quantitative agreement with simulations of the non-interacting charge susceptibility. A detailed analysis and decomposition of the simulations reveal the intra-band origin of this low-energy excitation, confirming it as the Lindhard continuum. Our results establish ultra-soft resonant inelastic X-ray scattering as a momentum-resolved probe of the fermiology in metals.

title: Terahertz field-induced giant symmetry modulations in a van der Waals antiferromagnet
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Strong-field terahertz (THz) excitations enable dynamic control over electronic, lattice and symmetry degrees of freedom in quantum materials. Here, we uncover pronounced terahertz-induced symmetry modulations and coherent phonon dynamics in the van der Waals antiferromagnet MnPS3, in which inversion symmetry is broken by its antiferromagnetic spin configuration. Our time-resolved second harmonic generation measurements reveal long-lived giant oscillations in the antiferromagnetic phase, with amplitudes comparable to the equilibrium signal, driven by phonons involving percent-level atomic displacements relative to the equilibrium bond lengths. The temporal evolution of the rotational anisotropy patterns indicates a dynamic breaking of mirror symmetry, modulated by two vibrational modes at 1.7 THz and 4.5 THz, with the former corresponding to a hidden mode not observed in equilibrium spectroscopy. These effects arise in part from a field-induced charge rearrangement mechanism that lowers the local crystal symmetry and couples to the phonon modes. We uncover a long-lived field-driven response with a complex THz polarization dependence, consistent with a metastable state of reduced symmetry. Through comparison with simulations, we interpret this response in terms of a potential antiferromagnetic-to-ferrimagnetic transition. Our results establish an effective field-tunable pathway for driving excitations otherwise weak in equilibrium.

title: Light as a Switch: EPR Evidence for the Wavelength-Modulated Generation of Intrinsic and Defect-Associated Ti3+ Centers in a MUV-10(Ca) Framework
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Titanium-based metal–organic frameworks (Ti-MOFs) are widely investigated for their potential in photocatalytic applications owing to their unique structural and electronic properties. However, the local identity of long-lived photoinduced Ti(III) species remains unresolved. In this study, the nature of photogenerated Ti(III) species in the stable Ti-MOF MUV-10(Ca) was examined by electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectroscopy. The results of X- and Q-band (9/34 GHz) continuous wave (CW) EPR provided unequivocal evidence for the presence of two chemically distinct Ti(III) sites, with the selectivity of Ti(IV) photoreduction governed by the hydration state of the material and the wavelength of the incident light. Consolidation of CW EPR and 1H Davies electron-nuclear double resonance (ENDOR) data allowed us to clearly determine the structure of both centers: one associated with an ideal Ti2Ca2-cluster and another one assigned to the missing-linker defect of the MUV-10(Ca) structure. This first example of such hydration state and wavelength-controlled selectivity in photoactive Ti-MOFs contributes to a deeper understanding of the nature of photoactive centers in Ti-MOFs, highlighting the importance of defect engineering for advanced applications.

title: Supramolecular Enforcement of Planar Tetracoordinate Halides
abstract: ABSTRACT Planar tetracoordinate halides have been widely explored by quantum computational approaches but remain rare as deliberately targeted experimental motifs. Here we show that these geometries can be accessed by supramolecular enforcement, and challenge its connection to the VSEPR model. Bowl‐shaped calix[4]pyrrolato indium units preorganize four lithium ions into a confined Li 4 pocket that traps Cl − , Br − , and I − in strongly flattened to ideal planar tetracoordinate environments. Computational analysis of the parent tetrahedral [Li 4 X] 3 + units reveals small planarization energies that can be overcome by a charge‐attenuating host of appropriate shape. The experimental series shows that halide planarity is highly sensitive to subtle supramolecular effects, such as calix[4]pyrrolato doming and crystal packing, experimentally confirming the generally low angular deformation energies. The results establish supramolecular enforcement as a rational design principle for planar tetracoordinate heavier halides and show that such motifs are accessible outcomes of engineered electrostatic cavities.

title: Expanding the Chemical Space of Analytes in the 2G Crystalline Sponge Method: Size‐Compensation Strategy for the Structural Analysis of Low‐Polarity Small Molecules
abstract: ABSTRACT The second‐generation crystalline sponge (2G‐CS) is a novel type of crystalline sponge that incorporates hollow cages as molecular recognition modules within its crystalline framework. This advanced CS technology provides a versatile structural analysis technique applicable to a broad range of guest molecules, regardless of polarity, with molecular weights ranging from 300 to 1500. However, the method often fails when analyzing rather low‐polarity small molecules (MW 200–300) due to an “unfavorable chemical space,” where the host cavities are too large to facilitate sufficient host–guest interactions. Here we overcome this limitation by establishing a size‐compensation strategy based on cage‐mediated pair‐selective bimolecular recognition. By co‐encapsulating a target analyte with a shape‐complementary “modulator” (e.g., phenanthrene), we precisely tailor the cavity environment without the need for chemical modification of the host. This adaptive approach enabled the x‐ray structural determination of 24 of 30 low‐polarity C15 analytes, predominantly sesquiterpenoids, including absolute configuration determination for selected chiral analytes. This work translates a decades‐old molecular recognition phenomenon into a practical approach to crystallographic structure determination of low‐polarity sesquiterpenoids.

title: Anion‐Cation Targeted Regulation Enables Ultrafast and Stable Sodium Metal Batteries at Low Temperatures
abstract: ABSTRACT Anion‐dominated solvation and artificial interfacial engineering have been intensively pursued for low‐temperature sodium‐metal batteries (SMBs), yet they face constraints from temperature‐sensitive solvation dynamics and interfacial control. Here we propose anion‐cation‐targeted regulation via Sn(OTf) 2 that simultaneously constructs a solvent‐reinforced solvation structure and electrochemically induces an alloy‐based solid electrolyte interphase (SEI) (Na 15 Sn 4 ), which goes beyond the prevailing anion‐centric strategy to address the critical challenges of SMBs at subzero temperatures. Competitive Sn 2+ ‐Na + coordination excludes PF 6 − from the primary solvation sheath, while OTf − and the ether groups of diethylene glycol dimethyl ether (DEGDME) coupling foster a solvent‐dominated configuration, substantially reducing the Na + desolvation energy barrier at low temperatures. This design enables Na||Na 3 V 2 (PO 4 ) 3 cells to deliver a recorded 1050 cycles at −20°C and 20 C, and nearly 700 cycles at −50°C. Ah‐scale pouch cells sustain durable 450 cycles at −20°C, with a 6 Ah cell reaching 215 Wh kg −1 at 25°C (total cell mass). Our findings resolve the longstanding trade‐off between low‐temperature kinetics and stability in SMBs, offering a new design rationale beyond conventional interfacial engineering.

title: Unidirectional Hydrogen Migration Through Interfacial Engineering for Promoted Brønsted Acid Catalysis
abstract: ABSTRACT Though playing a critical role, the controllable and directional migration of reactive species in chemical reactions is still hard to achieve. Here, we propose an interfacial engineering strategy for constructing a hydrogen spillover nanodiode that channels hydrogen unidirectionally. Such a nanodiode design is materialized in a composite WO x /TiO 2 /Pt catalyst with spatially separated structure, where WO x and Pt particles are dispersed on the outer and inner surfaces of porous TiO 2 nanotubes, respectively. This nanodevice permits forward H migration (Pt→TiO 2 →WO x ) while suppresses the reverse path (WO x →TiO 2 ), as directly evidenced by in situ x‐ray absorption fine structure characterization under hydrogenation and H 2 generation reactions. This rectification behavior originates from the diode characteristics of the TiO 2 –WO x heterojunction, which hinders both proton and electron transfer from WO x to TiO 2 . Consequently, WO x /TiO 2 /Pt accumulates highly concentrated Brønsted acid sites in H 2 atmosphere and thus exhibits superior catalytic performance compared to the closely contacted WO x –Pt/TiO 2 catalyst. Up to 5.3 times higher liquid alkane yield has been achieved over WO x /TiO 2 /Pt relative to WO x –Pt/TiO 2 in the polyethylene hydrocracking reaction. This nanodiode design strategy is general and can be extended to other catalysts/species, offering mechanistic insight and boosting catalytic performance in diverse reactions.

title: Helical Multi‐Resonance Thermally Activated Delayed Fluorescence Emitters for High‐Performance Anti‐Quenching Narrowband Blue OLEDs
abstract: ABSTRACT Multi‐resonance thermally activated delayed fluorescence (MR‐TADF) has established a new approach for narrowband blue organic light emitting diodes (OLEDs), yet effectively suppressing intermolecular interactions especially at high doping concentrations while preserving the intrinsic narrowband emission remains a formidable challenge. Herein, a novel designing paradigm is proposed for achieving anti‐quenching narrowband emission in MR‐TADF molecules by embedding the indeno[2,1‐b]carbazole unit into the polycyclic aromatic hydrocarbon skeleton. The proof‐of‐concept emitter DT‐BON1 reveals a favorable twist angle of 31.8°, manifesting formation of helical architecture within MR core. As a result, the emission peaks and full width at half maximum show virtually no variation with changing doping concentration from 1 wt% to 20 wt%. Moreover, the photoluminance quantum yields exceed 90% even at 20 wt% doping concentration endowed by the outstanding anti‐quenching characteristics. The DT‐BON1 based OLEDs can achieve maximum external quantum efficiency (EQE max ) of exceeding 30%. Especially, the alleviated exciton quenching effects can be firmly demonstrated by marginally decreased EQE max values, attaining 29.2% in 10 wt%‐based OLEDs and 27.3% even in heavily doped devices (20 wt%), which is at a record high for MR‐TADF with blue emission at such high doping concentration.

title: Increased southward swings of the South Indian convergence zone under greenhouse warming
abstract: Extreme southward swings of the South Indian convergence zone can lead to severe rainfall and flooding in southern Africa. Here the authors show that climate change leads to an increase in the frequency and intensity of such swings.

title: Divergent anaerobic fates of biodegradable plastics in landfill leachate
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Biodegradable plastics (BPs) are increasingly promoted as sustainable alternatives to conventional polymers, yet their fate in landfills remains poorly understood. Here, we evaluated the anaerobic biodegradability of three BPs, polyhydroxybutyrate (PHB), poly(lactic acid) (PLA), and poly(butylene adipate-co-terephthalate) (PBAT), in landfill leachate under mesophilic conditions by quantifying carbon conversion to biogas. The BPs exhibited sharply contrasting degradation trajectories: PHB mineralized completely within 17 d, whereas PLA underwent substantial mineralization over 320 d (83.6%), extending beyond the well-established expectation of limited mesophilic degradation. In contrast, PBAT remained largely recalcitrant. Multi-omics analyses linked PHB and PLA depolymerization to the biofilm–polymer interface, with depolymerase transcription tracking their distinct degradation phases. Putative depolymerase homologs were widespread across recovered bacterial genomes, yet only a subset showed transcriptional support. This active fraction included multiple under-characterized lineages outside the taxonomic range of experimentally validated degrader genomes, revealing a marked disconnect between genomic potential and realized activity. Our findings show that anaerobic biodegradation outcomes in landfill leachate cannot be inferred from biodegradability labels or genomic potential alone, but emerge from polymer-specific depolymerization constraints and depolymerase transcription enriched at the biofilm–polymer interface.
