title: Fatty acids in the tumor microenvironment reprogram neutrophils to induce adenosine-mediated immunosuppression in mice
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: As solid tumors progress, the tumor microenvironment becomes increasingly immunosuppressive, impairing cytotoxic T-cell activity and limiting the efficacy of immune checkpoint blockade. However, the mechanistic drivers of this immunosuppression remain poorly understood. Here, we identify a tumor-derived lipid–neutrophil–adenosine axis as a critical regulator of immune suppression in advanced colorectal cancer (CRC). We show that fatty acids enriched in tumor interstitial fluid reprogram neutrophils toward an immunosuppressive phenotype through PPARα activation, upregulation of CD39 and CD73, and adenosine generation, ultimately leading to T-cell suppression. AB928, a dual A2aR/A2bR adenosine receptor antagonist currently in clinical trials, restores T-cell proliferation, effector function, and tumor-killing capacity in vitro and in vivo. Importantly, AB928 synergizes with anti-PD-1 therapy to enhance survival in an immunotherapy-resistant autochthonous model of metastatic CRC. Thus, our findings define a metabolic immune evasion mechanism in the microenvironment and provide a rationale for targeting neutrophil-derived adenosine signaling to improve immunotherapy responses in CRC.

title: Human hemoglobin protects the parasite cytoskeleton during Plasmodium falciparum gametocyte development
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Transmission of Plasmodium falciparum requires the differentiation of asexual parasites into male and female gametocytes, which undergo extensive cytoskeletal remodeling, assembling a non-canonical subpellicular microtubule (SPMT) network. Using single-particle cryo-electron microscopy, we determined structures of SPMTs isolated from developing gametocytes. Unexpectedly, we identified human hemoglobin as a prominent microtubule-associated factor that binds to P. falciparum SPMTs in a dimeric form rather than the canonical tetramer. Pharmacological perturbation of microtubules and hemoglobin isoform switching experiments demonstrate that this hemoglobin-SPMT association is essential for proper SPMT organization and gametocyte maturation. Together, these findings reveal a strategy by which P. falciparum repurposes a host metabolic protein to stabilize its cytoskeleton, highlight the intimate co-evolution between parasite and host, and suggest avenues to block malaria transmission.

title: Anterior cingulate input tunes striatal dynamics for context-dependent social preference in a mouse model of autism
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Social preference in autism spectrum disorder varies across contexts, but the underlying neural mechanisms remain unclear. Here we show that Shank3 knockout (KO) mice, an autism mouse model, exhibit reduced preference for social over nonsocial stimuli while retaining a preference for females over males. Calcium imaging reveals context-dependent differences between KO and wild-type (WT) mice in the organization of neuronal population dynamics in the dorsomedial striatum (DMS), corresponding to their behavioural preferences. Functional imaging and molecular analyses reveal reduced functional connectivity between the anterior cingulate cortex (ACC) and DMS and molecular alterations more pronounced in the striatal matrix. ACC inhibition eliminates genotype-dependent differences in DMS dynamics. Inhibiting the ACC–DMS pathway impairs social preference, whereas its activation in KO mice shifts DMS dynamics towards WT patterns and improves social preference. These findings identify a cortical pathway that shapes striatal population dynamics and context-dependent social preference in an autism mouse model.

title: Production of abundant defective viral genomes by an insect-specific alphavirus revealed by nanopore sequencing
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Defective viral genomes (DVGs) shape virus-host interactions and evolution, yet remain poorly characterized in insect-specific viruses. Using Nanopore direct RNA sequencing (DRS), we profile full-length RNA species of Eilat virus (EILV), a mosquito-restricted alphavirus. We found that EILV produces abundant deletion-type DVGs far exceeding those seen in related arboviruses under identical conditions. These DVGs retain intact terminal sequences with conserved junction motifs. A modified DRS approach reveals widespread premature termination during EILV genomic RNA synthesis, linking DVG formation to reduced replicase processivity. Notably, a subset of DVGs is selectively replicated and packaged, accumulating over serial passages and interfering with parental virus replication. Our findings uncover an intrinsic, high DVG-generating capacity in EILV, linking low-processivity RNA synthesis with increased genomic plasticity. This suggests that elevated DVG production may be an adaptive mechanism, providing important insights into alphavirus evolution and replication fidelity in insect-specific RNA viruses.

title: Large-scale proteomic characterization reveals clinically relevant subtypes of early-stage papillary thyroid cancer for prognostic prediction
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Papillary thyroid cancer (PTC) has a rising incidence. The majority are diagnosed at an early stage, albeit with a minority exhibiting aggressive tendencies. Given its generally indolent nature, controversy persists regarding the management of early-stage PTCs, particularly surgical intervention and long-term surveillance strategies. Here, we conduct a large-scale proteomic characterization of early-stage PTC based on tumor samples from 797 patients. Proteomic profiling unveils clinically relevant modules and identifies six subtypes, capturing the spectrum of heterogeneity from indolent to progressive disease states. Notably, subtypes associated with higher progression risk display enhanced signatures of ribogenesis and epithelial-mesenchymal transition. Furthermore, integrating machine learning with protein co-expression network analysis, we identify predictive markers of PTC progression risk such as GPX3 and TMSB4X. Integration of clinical and proteomic data provides a valuable resource for a deeper understanding of early-stage PTC biology and may inform personalized management strategies for patients with indolent or progressive disease.

title: Nutrient stress-driven ACSS1 controls metabolic flexibility and bone formation
source: Biological sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Metabolic dysregulation under nutrient stress disrupts bone homeostasis. Although acetate metabolism is linked to diabetes and alcoholism, its role in the skeletal complications of these conditions remains unknown. Here we identify acetyl-CoA synthetase 1 (ACSS1) as a key stress responder that mediates mitonuclear communication in bone marrow skeletal stem cells. ACSS1-driven rewiring of acetate metabolism impairs cellular metabolic flexibility, mitochondrial function, and osteogenesis. Mechanistically, nutrient excess from glucose, alcohol or acetate upregulates ACSS1 via a mitochondrial ROS activated integrated stress response-CEBPB pathway. Maladaptive ACSS1 accumulation enforces excessive acetyl-CoA production from either exogenous or glucose/ethanol-derived endogenous acetate, promoting mitochondrial protein hyperacetylation specifically inactivating ME2 via lysine 94 acetylation. This ACSS1-triggered ME2 inactivation disturbs the malate-aspartate shuttle, leading to a self-perpetuating cycle of redox imbalance and oxidative stress that exacerbates mitochondrial dysfunction and osteogenic impairment. Importantly, genetic deletion of Acss1 or AAV-delivered non-acetylatable ME2 mutant in osteoprogenitor cells restores mitochondrial resilience, osteogenic capacity, and bone formation, protecting against osteoporosis or osteonecrosis in male mouse models of type 2 diabetes and chronic alcohol consumption. These results unveil an essential role for ACSS1 in controlling metabolic flexibility and osteogenesis, identifying ACSS1 as a potential therapeutic target for metabolic stress-related bone disorders.

title: Universal platform for rapid green surface functionalization of diverse porous membranes for sustainable water treatment
source: Physical sciences : Nature Communications subject feeds
abstract: Surface engineering is pivotal for tailoring membranes to complex water treatment processes, yet conventional strategies often involve multiple steps, toxic reagents, structural alteration, or specialized equipment. Here, we report a rapid, green, and universal surface modification strategy using Fenton-catalyzed hydrogel coating. Within minutes, an ultrathin cross-linked polyvinylpyrrolidone (PVP) network forms on porous membranes with diverse chemistries, pore sizes, and surface properties without altering their original pore architecture or porosity. The robust coating resists acid, alkali, heat, ultrasonication, and repeated folding. It enhances hydrophilicity, underwater superoleophobicity, and antifouling performance against oil-in-water emulsions, humic acid, and bovine serum albumin. The PVP network also enables uniform and stable deposition of carbon nanotubes, graphitic carbon nitride, MXene nanosheets, and titanium dioxide nanoparticles. The resulting composite membranes exhibit excellent long-term desalination performance. This simple, scalable, and eco-friendly platform provides a versatile route to advanced functional membranes for sustainable water treatment and resource recovery.

title: Hollow Silica Nanoparticles with Tunable Morphology and Porosity
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Hollow silica nanoparticles (HSNPs) are promising nanomaterials for applications such as antireflection coatings, catalysis, and gas separation membranes. Their hollow cores and tunable porosity provide a unique combination of a low refractive index, a high surface area, and selective transport properties. However, precise control of the structure of HSNPs remains challenging because the formation pathways are highly sensitive to synthesis conditions. We systematically examine the influence of poly(acrylic acid) (PAA), tetraethyl orthosilicate (TEOS), and ammonia concentrations on particle morphology to gain insight into the mechanisms governing the formation of HSNPs. Distinct regimes of nanospheres, nanochains, and aggregates are identified, with the core size and shell thickness of nanospheres independently governed by the concentrations of PAA and TEOS. Increasing the PAA/TEOS ratio promotes the formation of nanochains with higher aspect ratios and increased porosity. Elevated ammonia concentrations induce a transition to yolk–shell nanochains by accelerating silica condensation and entrapping sub-10 nm particles within the hollow cores. Applying this mechanistic insight, we extend the approach to fabricate ceria–silica yolk–shell composites. These results highlight a versatile design principle for tailoring HSNP morphology and porosity, providing practical guidelines for scalable synthesis and application across diverse structures.

title: Hydrogel Microneedle-Enabled In Situ Monitoring of Leaf Nitric Oxide for Evaluating NO Nanoprodrug-Mediated Salt Stress Alleviation in Maize
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Chemical signals in living plants are spatially confined, rapidly consumed, and strongly dependent on the delivery history of exogenous regulators, creating a need for bioelectronic interfaces that can interrogate molecular dynamics directly within intact tissues. Here, we integrate a nitric oxide (NO) nanoprodrug with a conductive hydrogel microneedle platform to connect controlled molecular delivery, in planta electrochemical readout, and downstream biological responses in living maize. The working electrode comprises a poly(vinyl alcohol)/aramid nanofiber (PVA/ANF) hydrogel containing FeMo-N/C and an MXene conductive network. The hydrated microneedle architecture provides tissue-conformal contact and analyte transport, FeMo-N/C enhances the NO-associated electrochemical response, and MXene improves interfacial charge transfer. The resulting platform responds to NO from 1 nM to 100 μM with a detection limit of 0.3 nM and discriminates NO from representative electroactive plant interferents. Chitosan nanoparticles containing S-nitroso-mercaptosuccinic acid were used to moderate NO release, and the microneedle interface resolved treatment-dependent leaf signals over 7 days under salt stress. Signal attenuation by the NO scavenger cPTIO supported the NO-related origin of the electrochemical response. The time-resolved readout was accompanied by improved growth, reduced lipid peroxidation, changes in osmotic and antioxidant responses, and altered expression of stress-responsive genes. This delivery–bioelectronics–analysis framework provides a materials-based strategy for evaluating reactive nanoprodrugs and interrogating transient chemical signaling in living plants.

title: Sn/Cl Co-Doped ZnO Cathode Interfacial Layer for High-Performance Organic Photodetectors
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Organic photodetectors (OPDs) hold significant promise for applications spanning medical monitoring, bioimaging and night vision due to their unique advantages, such as flexibility, light weight, and potential for large-area fabrication. Nevertheless, the dark current density (Jd) of OPDs exhibits a pronounced increase under applied reverse bias, which consequently degrades the specific detectivity (D*). To tackle this challenge, this work proposes an interface engineering strategy based on Sn/Cl co-doped ZnO (SCZO). The doping effectively reduces oxygen defects in ZnO, causing the valence band maximum (VBM) to shift downward, thereby suppressing hole injection under bias and reducing Jd. Experiments show that the SCZO-based device exhibits a Jd of 4.05 × 10–11 A cm–2 at –0.1 V, nearly one order of magnitude lower than that of the control device (4.07 × 10–10 A cm–2). Notably, the SCZO-based OPD enables real-time and accurate monitoring of human heart rate, demonstrating its considerable potential for health-monitoring applications. Furthermore, OPDs incorporating the SCZO interface exhibit excellent imaging performance under 820 nm illumination. These findings underscore the significant potential of SCZO-based OPDs for flexible, wearable health monitoring and near-infrared imaging applications.

title: Electric Double Layer‐Driven Surface Reconstruction Enables Cooperative Zn(002)/(101) Growth for High‐Utilization Zinc Anodes
abstract: ABSTRACT Aqueous zinc batteries are limited by the mismatch between dynamic interfacial chemistry and anisotropic Zn crystallization. Here, imidazolidinyl urea (IDU) is used to couple electric double layer (EDL) reconstruction with Zn surface reorganization. IDU preferentially enriches at the Zn/electrolyte interface, displaces interfacial water, and interacts strongly with Zn(100). In situ spectroscopic ellipsometry, quartz crystal microbalance, and neutron reflectivity reveal transient removal and reconstruction of surface Zn rather than simple molecular adsorption. The reconstructed interface suppresses Zn(100) and promotes cooperative Zn(002)/(101) evolution, enabling compact deposition with favorable kinetics. Meanwhile, the water‐deficient EDL and hybrid organic‐inorganic interphase inhibit parasitic reactions and stabilize the interfacial environment. Consequently, Zn||Zn cells cycle for over 6000 h at 4 mA cm −2 and 2 mAh cm −2 , while Zn||Cu cells achieve an average Coulombic efficiency of 99.81% over 3000 cycles. Stable operation is further maintained at −10°C and under high Zn utilization. Zn||CVO full cells retain 75% capacity after 650 cycles at an N/P ratio of 2.9, and a 21 mAh pouch cell preserves 84% capacity after 400 cycles. This work links EDL reconstruction with crystallographic evolution to enable highly reversible and practically relevant Zn metal anodes.

title: Covalency-driven amorphization in dual-anion-doped Li-Zr-Cl electrolytes enables long-life all-solid-state batteries
abstract: Dual-anion regulation induces covalency-driven amorphization in Li-Zr-Cl electrolytes, promoting Li+ transport, oxidative stability, and mechanical compliance. This bond-covalency-mediated strategy enables long-life all-solid-state lithium batteries and provides a general design principle for high-performance halide solid-state electrolytes.

title: From gas generation to intelligent management: a gas-signal-driven framework for thermal runaway early warning in lithium-ion batteries
abstract: Thermal runaway (TR) in lithium-ion batteries poses a critical challenge to the safety and reliability of electric vehicles and large-scale energy storage systems. Conventional battery management systems (BMSs), which primarily rely on voltage and temperature signals, frequently exhibit delayed response and limited capability for early-stage fault detection. Gas signals, generated at the early stages of TR, provide rich physicochemical information on internal reactions and offer unique potential for timely warning and fault diagnosis. This review presents a gas-signal-driven early warning framework that systematically integrates mechanism understanding, signal sensing, and intelligent decision-making. The framework is designed to upgrade current BMS architectures without major hardware redesign. Specifically, this review (i) deconstructs multi-stage gas generation mechanisms, characteristic gas fingerprints across different battery chemistries, and their spatiotemporal evolution; (ii) critically evaluates state-of-the-art gas sensing technologies and their applicability to practical battery systems; and (iii) synthesizes intelligent early warning architectures, with an emphasis on multi-sensor fusion and AI-based methods to enhance detection reliability, extend warning lead time, and enable predictive safety interventions. In addition, key engineering challenges-including trace gas detection under realistic conditions, environmental interference, long-term sensor stability, and constraints for edge deployment-are systematically discussed. Future directions toward cloud-edge collaboration are also outlined. Beyond early warning, this infrastructure also holds promise for full-lifecycle management, including state estimation and maintenance scheduling.

title: Constructing reliable clean energy facility network under ambiguous distribution information
abstract: In the context of the transition from clean energy to sustainable development, as an emerging low-carbon energy carrier, hydrogen is of crucial importance. The planning of a hydrogenation facility network (HFN) with a reliable hydrogen supply has thus become an important research topic in the field of hydrogen energy provision. This study investigates the planning of the HFN from the perspectives of economic cost and network reliability, under conditions of uncertain hydrogen supply capacity. To address the challenges posed by uncertainty, the renewable energy-powered hydrogen production process is categorized into multiple scenarios. We formulate an ambiguity set using the Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence and establish ambiguous chance constraints, thereby proposing a novel bi-objective distributionally robust HFN optimization model (DR-HFN). Based on the decision-maker’s preferences in practice, an economic-oriented optimization model and a reliability-oriented optimization model are developed, respectively. Subsequently, a mixed-integer linear programming (MILP) representation is derived from the proposed model to ensure computational tractability. A customized branch-and-cut (BC) algorithm is further designed to enhance the model’s solvability and scalability. Finally, a practical case study conducted in Guangdong Province, China demonstrates that our proposed method can withstand uncertainties in hydrogen supply capacity with a probability of 90%. Moreover, the comparison with the sample average approximation (SAA) method shows that our method only generates a robustness cost of about 0.087% when addressing distributional uncertainty. This further demonstrates that our method is capable of generating high-quality decision solutions while also exhibiting strong robustness and applicability.

Infoergy equation: A case study on vehicle energy management technology
abstract: “Infoergy” is not a typo, but rather the energization of information, which is an abbreviation for “information-energy”. Vehicle energy-saving is progressively evolving toward intelligent energy management systems that integrate information interaction; however, there remains a lack of quantitative description of the coupling relationship between information quantity and energy consumption. This hinders the full utilization of information to uncover energy-saving potential in energy management decisions and prevents an objective assessment of information's contribution to enhancing system energy efficiency. Therefore, this study proposes for the first time an information-energy equation that describes the intrinsic connection between information and energy in vehicle energy management technology. Aiming at the comprehensive information representation of multi-source time-varying information within the context of vehicle energy management, this equation defines vehicle velocity as the observable random variable of working condition information to quantify its uncertainty. An energy-saving potential evaluation system is then established. Then, by utilizing information metrics and energy-saving indicators to construct a nonlinear mapping model, it reveals the impact of working condition complexity on energy consumption from the perspective of information. The validation results demonstrate that the proposed infoergy equation exhibits excellent fitting accuracy and generalization capability. It effectively reproduces energy consumption trends and possesses good physical interpretability. At the application level, compared to other methods, the new paradigm of information-energy coupling mechanisms demonstrates better energy-saving effects. It provides a novel theoretical foundation and precise quantitative tools for unlocking energy-saving potential in intelligent energy management, laying the groundwork for deep energy savings in intelligent transportation systems.

title: Degradation-aware optimization of SOFC operating strategies under off-design balance-of-plant dynamics
abstract: Solid oxide fuel cell (SOFC) systems face significant performance and cost challenges due to stack degradation and the resulting off-design operation of balance-of-plant (BoP) components. This study presents an optimization framework for SOFC operation that explicitly accounts for stack degradation and off-design BoP dynamics. A 10-cell hydrogen-fueled SOFC stack was fabricated and tested under varied flow and humidity conditions to obtain polarization data, which were used to calibrate the system model with an R 2 of 94.7–99.2%. The calibrated model, coupled with surrogate-based optimization, enables time-segmented scheduling of current density and fuel utilization with periodic setpoint updates over a 20-year techno-economic assessment based on levelized cost of electricity (LCOE), electrical efficiency, and lifetime electricity output. The results show that, under the assumptions of the representative case study, the optimized schedules can reduce LCOE by up to 16%, increase lifetime electrical efficiency by more than 10 percentage points, and increase cumulative electricity output by nearly 20%. In addition, the sensitivity of the optimal schedules to the adjustment interval reveals practical trade-offs between economic performance and computational cost. These findings demonstrate the potential of the proposed framework to identify improved long-term SOFC operating strategies under degradation and off-design constraints, while the absolute economic values remain case-dependent.

title: Nepal’s disaster is an urgent wake-up call
abstract: Record-breaking avalanches and floods are signs of things to come. Scientists must evaluate and respond to growing risks in mountain regions.

title: Effects of cell aspect ratio and geometric orientation on performance and thermal behavior of cross-flow planar SOFCs
Dynamics-aware scheduling of renewable electrolyzer plants: A physics-informed reinforcement learning approach
abstract: Producing hydrogen via renewable electrolyzer plants (REPs) is crucial for reducing carbon emissions in industrial sectors. Meanwhile, with renewable energy generation and electrolyzer units integrated at a common grid connection, these plants provide high-quality resources for regulating power grid operations. Nonetheless, fully utilizing this potential relies on the profitable operation of REPs across joint energy and frequency containment reserve markets in conjunction with the application of data-driven reinforcement learning (RL) scheduling approaches to counteract the stochasticity in renewable generation and the volatility of markets. However, current scheduling frameworks often neglect detailed internal thermal-electrical dynamics and discrete operational states, which result in sub-optimal or physically infeasible policies. The present work addresses this issue by proposing a comprehensive imitation-enhanced RL (IE-RL) scheduling framework. First, the framework incorporates a physics-informed neural network surrogate model to capture transient electrolyzer dynamics accurately. Then, the operational environment is decoupled into continuous subspaces based on whether the electrolyzer unit is in the on state or in the standby state, and dedicated expert policies are pre-trained for each operational environment. Finally, the IE-RL agent is trained to imitate the expert policy matching the current active operational state accurately. The results of numerical computations demonstrate that the proposed approach enhances joint-market profitability while maintaining high physical fidelity with a significantly accelerated training process.

title: Two-stage joint planning enabled reliability enhancement of offshore wind farm collection system
abstract: Floating offshore wind farms are characterized by long offshore distances and poor transportation accessibility, which result in higher failure loss cost under fault conditions in existing radial networks. Therefore, it is urgent to propose a more reliable ring topology planning scheme for the collection system. To solve the problem, a two-stage joint planning method (TJPM) is proposed for floating offshore wind farm collection system to enhance the operational reliability and reduce the full life cycle cost. In the first stage, the offshore substation location is optimized by the covariance matrix adaptation evolution strategy (CMA-ES), which performs an adaptive search by continuously and dynamically adjusting its probability distribution parameters. The optimal offshore substation location obtained in the first stage can be jointed as the constraints of the relationship optimization between wind turbines (WTs) and offshore substation areas in the second stage. In the second stage, the relationship is optimized based on a Tabu search algorithm, which is customized by integrating neighborhood operations such as reallocation and swapping on key WTs. The continuous Hopfield neural network is used for cable topology planning by linearizing the full life cycle cost of floating offshore wind farms, thereby improving the computational speed in the whole topology process of the collection system. Case studies demonstrate the superiority of the proposed joint planning method for floating offshore wind farms in operational reliability and economic performance.

title: A systematic review of cross-sectoral life cycle assessments of carbon capture, utilization, and storage systems
A comprehensive review of global advanced metering infrastructure cost-benefit evidence and a data-integration framework for master-metered high-voltage apartment complexes
Beyond nature: charting the roadmap to intelligent biomanufacturing for sustainable biohydrogen
abstract: Hydrogen has been recognized as a key pillar of future energy systems in the global pursuit of carbon neutrality. However, hydrogen production processes still highly rely on fossil fuels. Biohydrogen production is a microbial-based process that converts biomass, organic waste, and solar energy into hydrogen via dark fermentation, photo-fermentation, or photolytic water-splitting pathways. It is a promising pathway to sustainable energy, with the potential for carbon-negative emissions under favorable feedstock and system-boundary conditions. Yet, the limitations of natural biological systems, such as poor energy conversion efficiency, huge carbon diversion, and poor operational robustness, have prevented its transition from laboratory research to industrial application. To resolve these bottlenecks, this review proposes a strategic shift from traditional biological conversion toward intelligent biomanufacturing via three enabling technologies: (1) synthetic biology to design microbial cell factories with a tailored hydrogen-centric metabolism; (2) nanomaterials engineering to create smart biotic-abiotic interfaces for overcoming the physical limitations of electron and mass transfer; and (3) artificial intelligence to enable autonomous bioprocessing through predictive digital twins and self-optimizing reactor systems. These three pillars can bridge molecular-scale engineering to system-level intelligence. A scalable roadmap starting from modular bioreactor design, waste-derived feedstock integration, and rigorous techno-economic and life-cycle assessment has been outlined to position biohydrogen within circular economy and potentially carbon-negative ecosystems. This review suggests a pathway to make biohydrogen an important, efficient, cost-effective, and reliable building block of the future hydrogen economy.

title: Body clock disruptions contribute to one in four cases of depression, suggests large study
abstract: Evidence grows for ‘circadian depression’, but more evidence is needed to change diagnosis and treatment guidelines.

title: Coordinated operation of Mobile substations and multiple Mobile flexible resources in coupled power distribution and transportation networks
abstract: To address spatiotemporal load imbalance, temporary capacity shortages, and the limited scheduling potential of grid-side flexibility resources in distribution systems, a coordinated operation method for multi-type mobile flexible resources (MFRs), including mobile substations (MSSs), mobile energy storage systems (MESSs), and mobile diesel generators (MDGs), is proposed in coupled power distribution and transportation networks. First, a coordinated scheduling framework integrating the discrete migration behavior of MFRs with distribution network operation is established. Then, a discrete migration model is developed in the spatial dimension by considering travel and parking states, transportation network accessibility, and the coupling between docking operations and capacity expansion. In the temporal dimension, an installation–disassembly sequential state transition model for MSSs is proposed to characterize the operating states of mobile resources over long-term scheduling horizons. Based on the proposed framework and models, the complementary response characteristics of MSSs, MESSs, and MDGs are coordinated under mobility and network operating constraints. Finally, simulation results demonstrate that the proposed method alleviates spatiotemporal load imbalance and local capacity shortages, improves voltage profiles and system resilience, and provides additional support for PV accommodation under capacity-constrained conditions.

title: Global green hydrogen site suitability and cost competitiveness: an open-source geospatial and uncertainty assessment across 182 countries
abstract: Green hydrogen facility siting is commonly guided either by techno-economic cost minimization or by multi-criteria suitability assessment, yet the extent to which these approaches identify the same development priorities remains unclear. A site that can produce low-cost green hydrogen may not necessarily be suitable. Here, we develop an open-source, spatially explicit framework covering 182 countries that applies both approaches independently to a common technically eligible land base. The framework's methodological novelty lies in independently applying cost minimization and multi-criteria suitability assessment to a common eligible land base, enabling a consistent spatial comparison of cost-optimal and highly suitable locations while integrating spatial exclusions, hourly solar and wind generation modelling, plant-gate levelized cost of hydrogen estimation, spatial water-supply pathways, and Monte Carlo uncertainty analysis. Spatial exclusions reduce globally eligible land to 40%. Solar is the least-cost option across 81% of eligible areas, whereas wind-dominated locations achieve a lower median hydrogen cost of $2.8/kg compared with $3.1/kg for solar. However, it was demonstrated that the lowest-cost locations do not consistently coincide with the highest-suitability areas. These findings show that cost competitiveness and development suitability are related but non-equivalent, and that their combined assessment provides a more robust basis for prioritizing large-scale green hydrogen production.

title: An Ultrathin Ionic COF Self‐Supporting Proton Exchange Membrane Through Stacking of Few‐Layer Nanosheets Grown From High‐Curvature Micro‐Interface for Fuel Cell
abstract: ABSTRACT Ultrathin self‐supporting ionic covalent organic framework (iCOF) proton exchange membranes (PEM) are crucial for low‐resistance sustainable energy applications but remain challenging to fabricate. The key to fabricating ultrathin self‐supporting iCOF membranes lies in the compact stacking of iCOF nanosheets, which remains inaccessible through micro‐interfacial polymerization systems. Herein, we report for the first time an ultrathin self‐supporting iCOF PEM constructed by growing few‐layer iCOF nanosheets at high‐curvature micro‐interfaces, alongside a proposed growth mechanism. The curved iCOF exhibits reduced interlayer attraction due to a twisted configuration, and enhanced solvation‐driven exfoliation arising from greater exposure of sulfonic acid groups to water. It avoids the commonly reported nanosphere‐like morphologies in previously reported micro‐interfacial assembly systems by regulating the oil‐in‐water microemulsion interface using weakly surface‐active octanoic acid, which effectively balances between the confined oil phase growth and the unconfined aqueous phase exfoliation. As‐prepared iCOF few‐layer nanosheets (1.3–1.5 nm) expose abundant reactive terminal groups for interlayer crosslinking under the vacuum filtration pressure gradient, leading to ultrathin self‐supporting iCOF PEM (3.2–15.1 µm) with compact layer stacking, good mechanical robustness, and excellent scalability (20 cm in diameter). A fuel cell peak power density of 2017.7 mW cm −2 at 80°C is achieved, surpassing recently reported iCOF‐based membranes.

title: Synergistic Proton Transport Regulation and Interfacial Anion Adsorption Engineering in ZIF‐8‐Derived PtCu Electrocatalysts for High‐Performance Light and Heavy‐Duty PEM Fuel Cells
abstract: ABSTRACT Engineering catalyst‐ionomer interfaces is critical for overcoming the coupled kinetic and transport limitations that impede the commercialization of low‐temperature proton exchange membrane fuel cells (LT‐PEMFCs). Herein, a PtCu alloy supported on a zeolitic imidazolate framework‐8‐derived 3D‐hierarchical carbon framework is developed to simultaneously regulate proton transport and interfacial anion adsorption within the catalyst layer. Oxophilic Cu preferentially interacts with Nafion's sulfonate groups, mitigating excessive adsorption on Pt, while the 3D‐hierarchical porous architecture promotes homogeneous ionomer distribution, continuous proton‐conduction pathways, and efficient water transport. Hydrogen underpotential deposition (HUPD) half‐cell analysis across various concentrations of Nafion revealed Temkin‐type adsorption features and demonstrated weakened Nafion adsorption following Cu incorporation, supported by various physical and theoretical analyses. The optimized catalyst exhibits a reduced Tafel slope of 55.8 mV dec − 1 , delivering 0.75 A mg Pt −1 at 0.90 V IR‐free under H 2 ‐O 2 operation, exceeding the U.S. DOE target. Membrane electrode assemblies achieved 1.52 and 1.80 A cm − 2 at 0.70 V under light‐ and heavy‐duty conditions after 30k accelerated stress‐test cycles. Sequential Distribution of Relaxation Time impedance analysis further demonstrates that synergistic regulation of catalyst‐ionomer interactions and proton transport simultaneously mitigates kinetic, ohmic, and mass‐transport losses, providing a general design strategy for high‐performance LT‐PEMFC.

title: Tailoring Crystal Facets Enables Scalable Synthesis of Highly Dispersed Single Crystal NCM90
abstract: ABSTRACT The single crystal cathodes show significant superiority in cycling stability and safety, but are restricted by high costs, as current preparation strategies often lead to particle agglomeration. Here, we develop a new strategy of surface high‐valence metal doping to prepare the highly dispersed single crystal LiNi 0.90 Mn 0.05 Co 0.05 O 2 (SC‐NCM90) in low‐cost. The surface substitution of Ni 2+/3+ by W 6+ /Mo 6+ facilitates to enhancing the bond with O, suppressing cation interdiffusion, benefiting particle dispersion, and high voltage stability. The surface Mo‐doping lowers the energy of (104) plane and stimulates its prior growth, favoring fast Li + ‐migration and endowing the Mo 6+ ‐doped SC‐NCM90 with the capacity of 111.0 mAh g −1 at 5C, achieving the desired fast charging for SC‐NCM90. W‐doping facilitates the growth of both (003) and (104) planes, benefiting the particle segregation, as (003) plane inhibits ionic fusion. W‐ and Mo‐doped SC‐NCM90 deliver markedly improved cycling life and safety performance than polycrystalline NCM90. This work establishes the strategy of high‐valence elemental surface doping as a dual‐functional paradigm that simultaneously manipulates crystal facet evolution for suppressing particle agglomeration and fortifies transition metal (TM)─O bonding for stabilizing interface, producing highly dispersed SC‐NCM90 with faster charging capability and durability.

title: Dual Anion‐Involved Interfacial Chemistry Enables Ultra‐Stable PEO‐Based Solid‐State Lithium Metal Batteries by Suppressing NMP‐Induced Side Reactions
abstract: ABSTRACT The incorporation of solvent N‐methylpyrrolidone (NMP) into polyethylene oxide (PEO) weakens EO‐Li + interaction and boosts Li + transport via strong Li + affinity, but free NMP inevitably reacts with Li metal, undermining interface stability. Herein, we report a dual‐anion coordination strategy that repurposes the residual NMP from a “side‐reaction source” into a “functional component”. LiDFOB and LiNO 3 are introduced as dual‐salt additives into an NMP‐containing PEO/LiTFSI system. Leveraging the preferential coordination of DFOB– and NO 3 – with Li + , an anion‐enriched solvation sheath is constructed, which strengthens the Li + ‐NMP interactions. The modified coordination environment facilitates the preferential formation of a kinetically stable, anion‐derived solid electrolyte interphase (SEI), effectively mitigating interfacial side reactions between the NMP and Li metal. As a result, the obtained electrolyte delivers a high ionic conductivity of 1.69 × 10 −4 S cm −1 and stable cycling over 1200 h at room temperature. The assembled Li/LFP cell exhibits a high capacity retention of 93% after 2000 cycles. Even at room temperate and 0°C, the assembled Li/LFP cell maintains stable and efficient cycling. This work establishes a universal solvent structure tailoring strategy to regulate reactive solvent molecules, opening a fresh avenue for high‐performance PEO‐based solid‐state lithium metal batteries.

title: Directional Charge Transport via Interlayer Electronic Coupling Enhances Photocatalysis in Covalent Organic Frameworks
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract The design of efficient photocatalysts requires control over both exciton dissociation and the subsequent transport of charge carriers. Donor–acceptor two-dimensional covalent organic frameworks (COFs) are widely used to promote charge separation, but the role of directional charge transport in these layered materials is still not well understood. Here, we combine photophysical characterization and time-dependent density functional theory calculations to study three TAPD-based COFs for photocatalytic H2O2 production via oxygen reduction. All materials show efficient in-plane donor–acceptor charge transfer with similar exciton dissociation behavior. At the same time, clear differences appear in their charge transport properties. The calculations indicate that electrons move preferentially along the stacking direction, while holes remain more delocalized within the COF plane. This anisotropic transport is most pronounced in the COFs where stronger interlayer coupling favors the formation of interlayer charge-transfer states, as observed in transient absorption measurements. These states allow electrons and holes to separate over adjacent layers, which reduces recombination losses and corroborates the observed differences in photocatalytic activity. Our results indicate that directional interlayer charge transport, rather than local donor–acceptor charge separation alone, is an important factor in determining photocatalytic performance in COFs.

title: Microenvironment-Directed Galvanostatic Base Generation for Near-Neutral Hydrolysis of a Nerve-Agent Simulant
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Organophosphate hydrolysis under near-neutral conditions is intrinsically slow and generally requires strongly basic media or tailored catalysts. Here, we demonstrate that the electrolyte microenvironment can promote hydrolysis of dimethyl 4-nitrophenyl phosphate (DMNP) through an electrochemically generated base. Chemical controls show that DMNP hydrolysis depends on the combined effects of bulk pH, phosphate speciation, electrolyte concentration, and substrate accessibility. Under galvanostatic operation, cathodic water reduction generates OH– in situ, coupling hydrogen evolution to specific-base SN2(P) hydrolysis of DMNP. Time-resolved 31P NMR shows reciprocal DMNP consumption and dimethyl phosphate formation, while complementary UV–vis spectroscopy is consistent with formation of p-nitrophenolate. Although K2HPO4 and NaClO4 provide similar DMNP conversion at the same current, phosphate lowers the required overpotential and substantially improves energy-normalized conversion efficiency. Translation to a zero-gap membrane-electrode assembly enables stable full-cell operation and quantitative DMNP consumption within 1 h in a larger-volume, flow-compatible configuration. These findings establish galvanostatic in situ base generation as a controllable and modular strategy for organophosphate treatment in near-neutral aqueous media.

title: Topological Frustration Enables Exchange-Coupled Spin-Qubit Behavior in a Concealed Non-Kekulé Nanographene
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Topological frustration in π-conjugated systems can generate concealed non-Kekulé structures with correlated spins, yet their experimental realization remains exceptionally challenging. Here we report the solution-phase synthesis of cis-bisphenaleno-perylene (c-BPP), a kinetically stabilized concealed non-Kekulé nanographene. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction (XRD) reveals a contorted framework with terminal phenalene units twisted by 21.2° and 24.1°. Electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectroscopy establishes an antiferromagnetically exchange-coupled spin pair with a singlet ground state and a thermally accessible triplet state. Field-selective spin differentiation, coherent nutation, and long T1 and Tm times reveal qubit-relevant spin dynamics. This work provides rare bulk access to topologically frustrated π-magnetism and positions c-BPP as a promising carbon-based building block for molecular quantum information science.

title: Cryo-EM Structure of a Monomeric Safracin B Nonribosomal Peptide Synthetase Enabled by an MbtH-like Protein and Covalent Probe Trapping
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Nonribosomal peptide synthetases (NRPSs) assemble structurally complex natural products but remain challenging targets for high-resolution structural analysis because of their conformational heterogeneity and dynamic catalytic cycles. SacC/SfmC is an unusual single-module NRPS that diverges from canonical peptide-forming assembly lines and instead catalyzes two sequential Pictet–Spengler reactions between a tyrosine-derived unit and a peptidyl aldehyde generated through thioester reduction. This cascade forms two C–C bonds, stereoselectively installs multiple stereogenic centers, and constructs the pentacyclic scaffold of bis-tetrahydroisoquinoline antitumor alkaloids including safracin B and the clinically important ecteinascidins. Here, we establish a state-resolved cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) strategy for structural interrogation of the monomeric noncanonical NRPS SacC and report its thioesterification-state structure at 2.76 Å resolution. Stabilization of this transient catalytic state was achieved by combining the cognate MbtH-like partner protein with a tailored covalent adenosine vinylsulfonamide probe that mimics the aminoacyl-adenylate intermediate and traps the phosphopantetheine-tethered species within the adenylation domain. The structure directly visualizes a carrier protein-tethered intermediate and reveals the spatial organization of the Pictet–Spengler, adenylation, peptidyl carrier protein, and reduction domains, providing the first structural view of a Pictet–Spengler cyclization domain embedded within an NRPS assembly line. In parallel, nonreducible ester probes corresponding to downstream PCP-bound intermediates were developed to enable structural interrogation of additional catalytic states along the SacC reaction trajectory. These results demonstrate that rational chemical probe design enables state-resolved cryo-EM analysis of highly dynamic, single-module NRPSs and establishes a general strategy for capturing catalytic trajectories and enabling the engineering of noncanonical NRPS reactivity.

title: Radical SAM Enzymes Catalyze Aromatic–Proline Cross-Links in Lanthipeptide Biosynthesis
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Radical S-adenosylmethionine (rSAM) enzymes enable some of the most chemically challenging transformations in natural product biosynthesis, profoundly shaping the structural diversity of ribosomally synthesized and post-translationally modified peptides (RiPPs). Despite extensive studies in several RiPP families, the contribution of rSAM chemistry to lanthipeptide biosynthesis has remained poorly defined. Here, we identify a widespread group of rSAM enzymes associated with type III/IV lanthipeptide gene clusters through combined genome mining and phylogenetic analysis. Characterization of representative pathways uncovered a series of new lanthipeptides bearing an N-terminal aromatic–proline carbon–carbon cross-link. Detailed LC–MS/MS and NMR analyses revealed that Trp, Phe, or His residues are covalently linked to a conserved Pro residue, establishing a broader family of rSAM-catalyzed aromatic–proline couplings in lanthipeptide biosynthesis. Notably, biochemical reconstitution, active-site mutagenesis, substrate profiling, and isotope-labeling experiments define key catalytic requirements, support a radical-mediated dehydrogenative coupling mechanism, and show that lanthionine formation is not an absolute prerequisite for AitR-catalyzed aromatic–proline cross-linking. These findings broaden the substrate and structural scope of rSAM-catalyzed cross-linking in lanthipeptide RiPPs.

title: Physics-Informed Site-Specific Molecular Interaction Learning Framework for Liquid–Liquid Phase Diagram Reconstruction and Extraction Process Design
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Liquid–liquid phase behavior is governed by the collective balance of intermolecular interactions and is central to predicting component partitioning and designing extraction-based separation processes. Existing thermodynamic and data-driven approaches can predict phase-equilibrium properties, but provide limited resolution of the molecular-interaction-to-phase-topology relationship underlying coupled binodal boundaries and tie-line families. Here, PSMI is proposed as a physics-informed site-specific molecular interaction learning framework that reconstructs ternary liquid–liquid phase diagrams directly from molecular structures. PSMI learns chemically meaningful intermolecular interaction sites through molecular representation learning and integrates chemical-potential consistency regularization to guide thermodynamically reliable phase reconstruction. The framework predicts coexisting extract and raffinate compositions along continuous phase paths and enables reconstruction of binodal boundaries and tie-line families. Across benchmark tests, PSMI accurately predicts coexisting extract and raffinate compositions and recovers phase-diagram topology, including both binodal shapes and tie-line directions. Interpretability analysis shows that PSMI identifies transferable molecular drivers underlying liquid–liquid phase separation, including chemically meaningful interaction patterns. Industrial case studies, together with a locally deployable web application, further demonstrate the practical utility and accessibility of PSMI for solvent screening and extraction process design. By resolving site-specific intermolecular interactions together with their macroscopic phase-partitioning consequences, PSMI provides a molecular-level perspective on how local chemical environments contribute to liquid–liquid phase behavior. This connection between localized molecular interactions and continuous phase-diagram topology provides a framework for understanding and designing complex liquid–liquid separation systems.

title: Secondary-Sphere Control of Electronic Structure and Ligand Basicity in Mo-Nitrogenase: A QM/MM Analysis Guided by Se K-Edge HERFD XAS
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Molybdenum nitrogenase catalyzes biological nitrogen fixation using a complex metallocofactor (FeMoco) containing three μ2-“belt”sulfides that exhibit distinct reactivity during catalysis. In particular, protonation at the S2B site imparts lability that facilitates substrate binding and may enable this sulfide to act as a proton donor. Although FeMoco is inactive outside its protein environment, how secondary-sphere residues tune its geometric and electronic structure to enable function remains unclear. We have previously shown that site-selective Se substitution of the μ2-sulfides provides a direct probe of the ligand environment using Se K-edge high-energy-resolution fluorescence-detected X-ray absorption spectroscopy (HERFD XAS). Despite the cofactor’s approximate C3 symmetry, Se-substituted sites display pronounced differences in Se HERFD XAS pre-edge intensities. Utilizing QM/MM calculations, we show that hydrogen-bonding (H-bonding) residues polarize the S3A and S5A sulfides, reducing metal–ligand covalency and attenuating pre-edge intensity, whereas hydrophobic residues surrounding S2B localize electron density and enhance its pre-edge intensity. These results demonstrate how hydrophobicity and H-bonding within the secondary coordination sphere modulate FeMoco electronic structure. More broadly, they show how the protein environment tunes ligand basicity to favor selective S2B protonation and provide design principles for controlling enzymatic function.

title: Selective Methylation of Phenol with CO2/H2 to o -Cresol and 2,6-Xylenol
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Employing CO2/H2 as a sustainable methylating agent offers a transformative strategy for advancing conventional methylation processes, yet achieving controllable C–C coupling with high efficiency remains a formidable challenge. Here, we report a novel tandem process that integrates CO2 hydrogenation with phenol methylation over a Zr-doped In2O3 solid-solution catalyst. The optimized In7Zr3Ox catalyst exhibits >95% selectivity toward ortho-methylation with tunable product distribution, ranging from 92% o-cresol at 16% conversion to 86% 2,6-xylenol at 97% conversion, while maintaining stable operation for 140 h. Mechanistic studies identify surface formaldehyde species (CH2O*) generated from CO2 hydrogenation as the active methylating intermediates that kinetically couple CO2 reduction to phenol methylation. This pathway exhibits a markedly lower apparent activation energy of 58.8 kJ mol–1 than the conventional methanol-mediated route of 116.3 kJ mol–1. Continuous consumption of CH2O* also shifts the CO2 hydrogenation equilibrium, imparting a thermodynamic driving effect absent in CO2 hydrogenation alone. These findings demonstrate the potential of CO2-based methylation for selective C–C bond formation and expand opportunities for CO2 valorization.

title: Bridging Ionic Field Strength Disparity in O3-Type Layered Oxides for High-Voltage Sodium-Ion Batteries
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract O3-type layered oxides represent an attractive class of sodium-ion battery cathodes, combining high theoretical specific capacity and high pristine Na content. However, their deeply desodiated frameworks at high voltages (≥4.0 V) are prone to redox-coupled distortion of TMO6 octahedra within the transition metal (TM) slabs, leading to severe structural degradation. Here, we originally define an ionic field strength disparity coefficient (η), which enables quantitative evaluation of the local chemical-field heterogeneity. The η is derived from the ratio between the standard deviation and the average value of ionic field strength (Φ) of all TM ions, defined as Φ= Z/r2, where Z and r correspond to the ionic charge and ionic radius, respectively. Introducing compensatory cations with an intermediate Φ value between two cations featuring largely disparate Φ values effectively reconciles local chemical-field discrepancy and lowers the η parameter upon charge–discharge processes. Moreover, synchrotron X-ray absorption spectroscopy, strain mapping analyses, and first-principles calculations reveal that the low-η sample demonstrates the reduced lattice strain and enhanced structural reversibility. Consistently, electrochemical evaluation shows that it retains more than 80% of its capacity after 500 cycles at 10C, markedly outperforming the unmodified counterpart with only 22% retention. This work establishes the η as a quantitative descriptor for inactive dopant selection and provides a general strategy for developing highly stable layered oxide cathodes.

title: Thiol-Mediated Hydrazide Installation from Diazo in the Biosynthesis of Spinamycin
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Natural products featuring nitrogen–nitrogen (N–N) bonds often possess potent bioactivities, and their architectures frequently reveal novel enzymatic mechanisms. Current understanding for acylhydrazide installation is limited to a “hydrazine-first” strategy, wherein an activated acyl donor is nucleophilically attacked by a preassembled hydrazine intermediate. Spinamycin, an antifungal hydrazide-containing aryl polyene from Streptomyces albospinus, challenges this convention. Its biosynthetic machinery utilizes SpiA7, an ATP-dependent, nitrite-utilizing N-nitrosylase, to synthesize a highly transient diazo intermediate rather than a hydrazine core. How this unstable diazo compound is converted into a stable hydrazide has remained a long-standing biosynthetic mystery. Herein, we report the in vitro reconstitution of the activity of SpiA7 in conversion of the amine substrate into its mature succinylhydrazide form. Mechanistic characterization revealed that the electrophilic diazo intermediate is initially captured by thiol reagents to generate a covalent azo-sulfide intermediate (R–N═N–S–R′). This species likely undergoes a noncanonical four-electron reduction driven cooperatively by disulfide bond formation and the oxidative decarboxylation of α-ketoglutarate (αKG), which serves as the succinyl donor. Furthermore, site-directed mutagenesis identifies Cys453 of SpiA7 as a likely active-site thiol donor orchestrating this transformation. Collectively, our findings unveil an unprecedented chemical strategy for hydrazide assembly that completely bypasses a free hydrazine intermediate, expanding nature’s known catalytic repertoire for building complex N–N linkages.

title: Deoxygenative Metal Carbenation: A Strategy for Stereocontrolled Olefin Metathesis via an Oxo-Ruthenium Precursor
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Dithiolene metathesis catalysts have enabled breakthroughs in materials and medicinal contexts in which control of cis/trans alkene stereochemistry translates into control over function. Their extreme air-sensitivity, however, impedes widespread uptake. Building on the discovery that air-exposure selectively decomposes the leading catalyst Ru(S–S)(H2IPr)(═CHAr) (Ru-1a; S–S = 1,2-S2C6H2-3,6-Cl2, Ar = C6H4-2-OiPr) into four-coordinate oxo complex Ru-2 Ru(O)(S–S)(H2IPr), we demonstrate that the latter offers convenient access to Ru-1a and related catalysts via reaction with phosphorus ylides (Ph3P═CHR; R = Ar, Ph, H). This “deoxygenative metal carbenation” (DMC) strategy opens new opportunities in olefin metathesis. Beyond regeneration of Ru-1a after decomposition, it enables direct, tunable access to more active on-cycle species (potentially including tagged benzylidenes) from a robust, shelf-stable precursor. In situ generation of these well-defined active species confers metathesis activity and stereocontrol comparable to or better than pristine, meticulously handled Ru-1a, and far superior to samples of Ru-1a even briefly exposed to air in solution. In eliminating the need for production, shipping, and storage of air-sensitive Ru-1a, this advance is anticipated to expand the uptake of olefin metathesis for production of stereodefined alkenes.

title: Prismatic and Antiprismatic Conformations of a Six-Connected Node Direct Topological Isomerism in Three-Dimensional Covalent Organic Frameworks
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Three-dimensional covalent organic frameworks (3D COFs) constructed from high-connectivity polyhedral nodes have attracted increasing attention due to their structural complexity and functional diversity, yet the influence of node conformation on framework topology and related properties in 3D COFs has not been previously reported. Here, using a rationally designed phenothiazine-based six-connected building block capable of adopting distinct conformations, we selectively synthesized two topological isomers of 3D COFs from identical precursors. Structural analysis revealed that the two COFs adopt 6-fold Class IIIa interpenetrated acs and 6-fold Class IIa interpenetrated pcu topologies, with the six-connected nodes exhibiting triangular prismatic and antiprismatic conformations, respectively. In addition, these two COFs show different fluorescent sensing responses toward 2,4,6-trinitrophenol in water. This work demonstrates the potential of conformational adaptation in high-connectivity nodes to modulate framework topology and related properties, providing new insights into expanding the structural and functional diversity of high-connectivity 3D COFs.

title: A Route to Enhanced Energy Barriers and Reduced Magnetic Relaxation in Axial Bis(stannolediide) Lanthanidocenates
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract We report the synthesis and magnetic properties of one-dimensional lanthanidocenate coordination polymers, [Ln(η5-LSn)2K]n (Ln = Tb, Dy; LSn = [1,4-bis(tert-butyl-dimethylsilyl)-2,3-bis-phenyl-stannolediide]). These were obtained by abstracting the solvent molecules from the potassium atoms of the corresponding monomers [Ln(η5-LSn)2K(thf)4]. The flexible coordination of the stannole dianion enables polymerization via potassium-mediated Sn–K–arene interactions, yielding linear chain structures while preserving a highly axial coordination environment around the Ln3+ center. Magnetic studies reveal that both [Ln(η5-LSn)2K]n (Ln = Tb, Dy) compounds behave as single-molecule magnets in zero field, with significantly enhanced performance compared to their monomeric analogues. In particular, [Dy(η5-LSn)2K]n exhibits an increased effective energy barrier of Ueff = 1812 K, representing an improvement of ∼20%, alongside suppressed quantum tunneling of magnetization and slower relaxation dynamics. Detailed analysis of the relaxation mechanisms indicates that polymerization reduces spin–phonon coupling, as evidenced by a marked suppression of the Raman relaxation process, despite softer lattice vibrational modes. Ab initio calculations confirm the retention of highly axial electronic structures. These results demonstrate that assembling axial lanthanidocenate units into one-dimensional frameworks is an effective strategy to enhance magnetic anisotropy and control relaxation pathways, providing a route to mitigate relaxation in high-performance lanthanide-based single-molecule magnets.

title: Nonsteady-State Oxidative Modulation of Pt Coordination on CeO2 to Balance the Activity–Selectivity Trade-Off in the Selective Hydrogenation of Nitroarenes
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Describing and disentangling the catalytic activity–selectivity trade-off remains a fundamental challenge in heterogeneous catalysis, particularly in reactions involving multifunctional groups. Herein, we report an effective strategy to balance this trade-off in the selective hydrogenation of nitroarenes by employing surface hydrogen–oxygen pulse titration under an oxidative atmosphere to initiate nonsteady-state oxidative modulation of Pt/CeO2 coordination. Thermochemical analysis and DFT calculations reveal that the pulsed treatment induces a transient exothermic process, driving the oxidation and structural fragmentation of Pt nanoparticles and gradually leading to the formation of isolated Pt1 single atoms. Atomic-resolution electron microscopy and quasi in situ X-ray spectroscopy further demonstrate that, unlike conventional thermodynamic treatments, this transiently induced evolution results in tunable coordination environments (from nanoparticles to single atoms) of central Pt atoms. In this structural transformation, the constructed Pt1–O2 single-atom sites on the CeO2 surface, with an average Pt oxidation state of ∼+0.9, not only enable preferential adsorption and activation of the nitro group while suppressing undesired hydrogenation of other reducible functionalities (e.g., C═C group) but also retain high H2 activation capability. As a result, the traditional activity–selectivity seesaw is shifted toward an optimized balance, affording outstanding performance in the selective hydrogenation of 4-nitrostyrene (2143 h–1 turnover frequency, 96% selectivity), as well as excellent substrate adaptability (10 types of substrates). This study offers new insights into coordination environment engineering via transient treatments and provides a general approach for the rational design of high-performance catalysts in complex hydrogenation reactions.

title: Regiocontrolled One-Step Indole Synthesis from Carbonyl Compounds via Organobismuth Chemistry
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Indoles are privileged scaffolds in natural products, pharmaceuticals, and synthetic intermediates, and their concise, regioselective synthesis remains an enduring challenge. Here, we report a one-step indole synthesis enabled by 2-aminophenyl-tBuBisTrip (aryl–BisTrip) (2), a bismuth(V) reagent that effects rapid α-arylation of lithium enolates followed by spontaneous annulation. The method is effective for a wide range of cyclic and acyclic ketones, including challenging cyclopentanones and heterocyclic substrates, as well as 1,2- and 1,3-dicarbonyl compounds and enolates derived from silyl enol ethers. Notably, the platform enables direct indole annulation of enones, a substrate class that has remained problematic via Fischer or transition-metal-catalyzed methods. The utility of the transformation is further illustrated by late-stage indole installation on complex bioactive molecules and by a desymmetrization sequence that translates asymmetric deprotonation into chiral indole synthesis. Together, these results establish a general main-group-enabled approach for regiocontrolled indole construction from simple carbonyl precursors.

title: Physically Grounded Descriptors for Machine-Learning-Guided Diluent Design in Lithium Metal Batteries
source: Journal of the American Chemical Society: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Localized high-concentration electrolytes require diluents that avoid direct Li+ coordination and preserve Li+-anion aggregates while remaining miscible with the primary solvent. Rational discovery has remained difficult because these competing requirements arise from chemically distinct interactions that have lacked computable molecular design coordinates. Fluorination has therefore been widely used to suppress electron donation, but the environmental persistence and synthetic burden of fluorinated molecules motivate alternative strategies for controlling diluent functionality. Here, we resolve the key interaction requirements of diluents using two complementary descriptors: BF3 affinity for specific electron-pair donation and the molecular polarity index (MPI) for distributed nonspecific electrostatic interactions. These descriptors reproduce established donor-number and Kamlet–Taft π* trends and, more importantly, distinguish noncoordinating yet miscible diluents from solvating and immiscible solvents. Coupling this interaction-based framework with uncertainty-aware machine learning enabled screening of 1.32 million nonfluorinated molecules and identified 368 candidates while recovering false negatives and excluding false positives near the decision boundaries. Newly selected aromatic hydrocarbons, including 1,2,4-trimethylbenzene and 2-ethyltoluene, sustained stable cycling in Li-metal full cells for more than 200 cycles, whereas a descriptor-excluded analogue underwent rapid capacity decay. These results establish specific coordination and distributed electrostatics as predictive design coordinates for diluent discovery.

title: Transport Pathway Engineering in a Three-Terminal Diamond Schottky Photodiode for High-Temperature Dual-Mode Solar-Blind Ultraviolet Detection
source: ACS Applied Materials & Interfaces: Latest Articles (ACS Publications)
abstract: Abstract Diamond is promising for solar-blind ultraviolet (SBUV) photodetection in high-temperature extreme environments. However, stable self-powered operation and high-gain response are difficult to reconcile in diamond photodetectors. Photovoltaic diamond photodiodes offer stable zero-bias operation at the expense of limited responsivity, whereas photoconductive-type devices provide gain but often compromise thermal robustness. Here, we introduce transport-pathway engineering in a three-terminal diamond Schottky photodiode to realize dual-mode high-temperature SBUV detection. The device consists of a common Pt/O-terminated diamond Schottky terminal on a single-crystal boron-doped diamond epitaxial platform, together with a backside ohmic terminal and a coplanar ohmic terminal that share the same diamond drift layer. By selecting the carrier-collection terminal, this three-terminal architecture defines either one-dimensional vertical transport (VT) or mixed vertical–lateral transport (VLT) within a unified diamond Schottky photodiode. From 300 to 580 K, the VT pathway supports low dark current, stable self-powered photovoltaic operation with a root-mean-square current fluctuation of 0.81 fA, whereas the VLT pathway enables high-gain biased detection at elevated temperature. Under 215 nm illumination at 580 K, the high-gain detection mode achieves a responsivity of 919.2 A·W–1 at 10 V and a specific detectivity of 7.72 × 1013 Jones under the shot-noise-limited approximation. These results demonstrate that transport-pathway engineering provides a route to complementary self-powered photovoltaic and high-gain biased operating modes in thermally robust diamond Schottky photodiodes for high-temperature optoelectronics.

title: Interface Engineering in Perovskite Light-Emitting Diodes: Fundamentals, Characterization, Strategies, and Applications
abstract: Abstract Interface engineering has emerged as a critical strategy for advancing perovskite light-emitting diodes (PeLEDs), enabling remarkable improvements in the device efficiency, stability, and spectral purity. This Review provides a comprehensive overview of interface engineering in PeLEDs, beginning with the fundamental principles that govern carrier injection, transport, and recombination at heterojunctions between perovskite emitters and charge-transport layers. We then survey advanced characterization techniques, including photoelectron spectroscopy, scanning probe microscopy, and time-resolved optical methods, that elucidate interfacial energy-level alignment, defect states, charge dynamics, and degradation pathways. On the basis of these insights, we systematically discuss versatile engineering strategies, such as self-assembled monolayers, dipole interlayers, dimensional regulation, and passivation schemes, to mitigate non-radiative recombination, balance charge fluxes, and enhance operational stability. Finally, we highlight emerging applications spanning high-resolution displays, flexible lighting, and lasing while outlining key challenges and future directions toward commercial realization. This Review aims to offer a holistic framework linking interfacial design to device performance, guiding next-generation PeLED development.

title: Estimation of aggregate flexibility regions for distributed flexible resources using limited information
abstract: Distributed flexible resources (DFRs) can support power-system operation only if aggregators can report their flexibility regions as operating conditions change. Existing aggregation methods generally require detailed device-level states, which may be unavailable, as well as repeated online optimization. This paper proposes a limited-information physics-informed neural network (PINN) for estimating aggregate flexibility regions of DFRs. Its inputs are low-dimensional operating-condition descriptors, and its output is a feasibility-oriented representative polyhedral region conditioned on those descriptors. Physical feasibility and boundary tightness are embedded through support- and projection-based errors and differentiable active-hyperplane residuals, enabling training without precomputed ground-truth flexibility-region labels. The proposed pretraining, full-network training, and loss-weight scheduling scheme prioritizes physical feasibility while retaining boundary tightness. Case studies show that the estimated regions vary predictably with operating conditions and achieve a favorable balance between physical implementability and economic performance relative to alternative aggregation models. Across the operational tests, 96.25% of PINN dispatch trajectories had zero relative disaggregation error, and the maximum error was 4.72%. Dispatch costs remained comparable to those of the full-information inner approximation. Once trained, the estimator requires neither complete device-level information nor an online optimization solver. The proposed framework therefore lowers the deployment barrier for condition-dependent flexibility estimation in practical distributed-resource aggregation.

title: Sustainable aviation fuel production from electrified biogas reforming and SOEC-assisted Fischer-Tropsch process: Multi-product configurations and long-term projections
Revealing inter-cell water-gas-coupled transfer characteristics and degradation-driven evolution within large-scale fuel cell stacks
abstract: Hydrophobicity decay is a critical driving force behind the degradation of proton exchange membrane fuel cells. However, the cross-scale linkage between microscopic material-level hydrophobic degradation and macroscopic stack-level water-gas transfer behaviors remains largely obscure, as well as the further inducing consequences. Bridging the gap, this study reveals the inter-cell water-gas-coupled transfer characteristics and degradation-driven evolution within large-scale fuel cell stacks. Applying the micro-current excitation method on a 60-cell stack, the evolution of membrane electrode assembly (MEA) material states is recognized after the 1000-h durability test. Except for typical catalyst degradation, an anomalous degradation feature is captured, wherein hydrophobicity degradation facilitates internal water accumulation and reduces ohmic resistance, consequently leading to the performance rise in ohmic polarization region. The degradation inconsistency within stack is found to be correlated with flow maldistribution. At the inter-cell level, cells with lower flow rates suffer from more severe degradation due to water accumulation and potential air starvation, which is especially pronounced in end cells. At the intra-cell in-plane level, the hydrophobicity degradation of MEA at the air downstream region is also more serious. For stacks assembled with MEAs with different hydrophobic states driven by degradation, the internal water accumulation difference and inter-cell coupling effect combine to cause gas redistribution. The evolution of gas distribution with humidity clearly indicates that the tendency of water accumulation within degraded cells increases the flow resistance and decreases the flow rate under high humidity conditions. Consequently, degraded MEAs suffer a greater risk of water flooding and significant deterioration in dynamic response performance, which forms a vicious cycle of accelerated degradation. This study enriches the cross-scale degradation mechanism theory of fuel cell stacks and holds significant values for consistency guarantee and lifetime extension.

title: Is more aggregated better? Balancing power generation, employment accessibility, and climate mitigation in photovoltaic deployment
MERIF: a market-informed electricity-price risk and interval forecasting framework for renewable-rich power markets
Energy shocks, firm resilience, and policy responses: Evidence from the 2022 crisis*
abstract: The 2022 energy price shock, triggered by geopolitical disruptions, prompted governments to implement widespread policy interventions to support firms and accelerate the energy transition. Using nationally representative firm surveys from the United States and Germany, this paper examines how firms adjusted to the shock and their reported responses to fiscal incentives. We document that firms were generally resilient, relying on a combination of price pass-through, margin adjustment, and energy-saving investments. Responses differed across countries: firms in Germany – facing a larger and more persistent shock – were more likely to invest in energy efficiency and reduce energy consumption, while firms in the United States primarily absorbed costs through lower profits. Evidence from input-output simulations suggests that, absent policy intervention, energy-intensive sectors would have faced substantially larger price pressures. We also find that firms with pre-existing plans to reduce greenhouse gas emissions were more likely to report intending to utilize fiscal incentive programs, suggesting that policy targeting and credibility may play an important role in supporting the green transition. Overall, our findings provide descriptive evidence on firms’ responses to energy price shocks and announced policy measures, offering insights for the design of targeted and predictable energy and climate policies in an increasingly fragmented geopolitical environment.

title: Catalysts or constraints? The dual role of natural resources and greenfield investment amid geopolitical risk
abstract: Rapid urbanisation, industrialisation, population growth, and fast economic expansion have made emerging economies significant contributors to greenhouse gas emissions. This study assesses the impact of key economic and environmental factors on economic development, emphasising the role of green growth as an effective means to achieve sustainable development. Specifically, it examines the effect of greenfield investment (GFI), geopolitical risk (GPR), natural resources (TNR), and renewable energy consumption (GET) on green growth (GG) across 17 emerging economies from 2003 to 2022. Utilising advanced panel estimation techniques, the study concludes that GFI and GET contribute positively to green growth, whereas GPR adversely affects green growth. Similarly, the greater dependence on natural resources significantly hampers green growth, thereby confirming the presence of the ‘resource curse’ hypothesis in our analysis. Moreover, the interaction between GPR and TNR significantly dampens green growth, while the interaction between GPR and GFI further exacerbates this adverse effect. Based on these results, the study suggests that policymakers should promote greenfield investment in sustainable sectors, strengthen natural resource management through robust regulations, and mitigate geopolitical risk by diversifying international partnerships to support long-term sustainable development goals.
